Firstly, I must admit I was spoiled by playing "Nightmares from the Deep 2: The Siren`s Call" first. The 3D renders aren't as smooth and you can't use the map to jump to locations. One thing it doesn't have like that game - thankfully - is no collectibles to find along the way.
Apart from the odd 3D, it's mostly a good looking, nice sounding game with decent puzzles. It's really hard for me to articulate any particularly good parts so I have to indulge in some criticism.
There are 2 sections that involve moving around objects that are weird and unintuitive. Too many pieces, too many large pieces and pieces will often jump back or lie somewhere close.
Elevator gets annoying. You have to stop at each floor, waiting a second or so for the door to open till you can continue. Particularly weird is that you can't control its direction so at one point in order to go up 1 floor, you need to go down first then up 2 floors. Aestetically annoying is that you can't shut the panel once you've fixed it...
Story seemed dubious at first but does gets explained near the end.
Jump scares not particularly scary for me, especially the first one.
Some hidden object clues are'nt clear but that's to be expected. One I really didn't approve of was "sugar bowl". I did an Image Search for that and it did NOT come up. What it should have been is "sugar dispenser".
Some achievements mean you'll have to play the game at least twice: once for the hidden objects and once for the dominos. Both times on Expert Mode. Else, like me, you'll have to play it about 5 times.
Speaking of Expert mode, Hiding HO areas is cruel especially considering they're repeated in some. Also for the reason that some interactive areas are just for flavour text. In fact, one is repeated AND has flaour text. I had to use the hint twice because there's no logical reason to go back a specific area and click on it again, especially if it's not nearby.
I managed to get all the achievements in 8 hours without a walkthrough so I'm satisfied with that.

I really wanted to like this game, really did. Back when Starbound was on Kickstarter, I couldn't keep my hype, everything looked so interesting, so many good ideas and concepts, some of those created by fans (like the Poptops).
When the beta came out, I was so happy and went to play immediately. My first impressions were that the game just felt so boring, and exploring the universe felt really empty and barren.
At the time, I thought it was ok, the game was only at beta, I thought they would think a lot more to what could be some good changes to the game, specifically to the races. One of the Kickstarter stretch goals ($500,000), were the race of Novakids, which are “interstellar gas-bag people”, but now, this race is nothing but a reskin of the player model. This is only an example of the concepts that were dumbed down to something so simple and tasteless.
The beta continued being this boring, wasted potential of a game. At a certain point of the beta (which took really long) they added quests to the game. These too felt really obnoxious to do; quests like "fetch quests" or "escort quests", things that you don't expect to do in a space-exploring game. But these were only the "sub-quests" of the game, so you could pass the time doing meaningless things, they added "missions" as well. Missions were nothing more than going through a lot of bad guys, waving your weapon, and defeating an underwhelming boss.
The pacing of the updates goes without saying; the beta was so slow, any annoying bug or glitch took ages to be fixed or to be removed. There were many delays for the release date and many unkept promises.
When they added "upgrades" to your ship, I got kind of excited wondering if this could be something cool, such as cannons for your ship, more gadgets for your ship, but instead you could only expand your ship to add more furniture, when you fully "upgrade" your ship it just feels like a huge empty metal box.
Finally, when the game came out, I was shocked at what the game has become. I am embarrased to say that I enjoyed more the beta than the final product. The "main storyline" is nothing more than the "missions" that I mentioned before, the pacing of the game feels sluggish and not very compelling to continue digging through the planets and exploring, for me it felt like there was no real objective because; the intention of the game that is exploring, felt repetitive. Combat feels slow and clunky, movement feels floaty, the new "hotbar" looks and functions really badly compared to the beta one. There are still some bugs, which I can forgive, but the game still feels unfinished and rushed.
As a sandbox, space-exploring game, Starbound is, in my opinion, a 4/10 game. It's really disappointing to see something that looked so complex and interesting die like a shallow abomination.

It's just bad... like really really bad. You're never sure if it's trying to be funny, or trying to be so bad that it's funny, and it never is actually funny. Side note, the "developers" of the game said that the majority of kimulator lies in the minigames, of which I could only stomach one. In this minigame, you play as the easter bunny (which has a very strong relation Kim Jong Un because reasons). As the easter bunny, you do some basic platforming across a bridge with missing planks. You then fall off the bridge into the ocean (because you suck at platforming) and you don't respawn. So, the only minigame I tested was broken.
Another side note: I would be more sympathetic to the "developers" if they had actually tried. The only place they tried were the cutscenes, which can't hold up the whole game. This could have worked as a 2D top down shooter, which would've been easy to make, especially in the sprite department, which the person who did the cover art seems to have at least some skill in.

I don't have anything against this sort of game really. Hidden Object games are a fun casual experience from time to time. My problem with the endless flood of these things on steam is that they aren't very good. The art is nice (barring the characters themselves) and the object finding is good enough but each game lacks anything to make it stand out from the others.
The best Hidden Object games in my mind remain the I-Spy ones, Treasure Hunt and Haunted House in-particular. They had simple goals but they were fun to pursue. Each Hidden object was a good time and clicking on things made them animate and made a simple game that much more entertaining. In this game everything just fades out of existence when you click on it. This makes each puzzle a chore instead of an experience.
The I-Spy games were also made or kids in mind so the goals were pretty simple, escape the house, find the treasure etc. However these were fun and relate-able in the sense that they were likely things kids imagined on their own. These games opt for some overly complex bull crap story with no real substance whatsoever. They choose to have characters with backstories and what not and still every one of them feels and sounds entirely disinterested at all times.
The other big problem I have here is backtracking. Sending the player all over this needlessly large environment to either pick up loose objects or do the same hidden object puzzles with different items to find. In I-Spy backtracking was done once at the end of the game to find hidden clues inside each puzzle that linked together. This was a really cool reason to backtrack because it meant the treasure, key, or whatever had been in plain sight all along. Here its just another chore to get another item so i can proceed to go to another puzzle.
Plus as far as this story goes... I defeated the dumb evil sea monster by literally messing up his drawing on the floor. That's what we call a payoff right there.

Abyss will seem very familiar to a lot of us, there is clearly a lot borrowed from Rapture (Bioshock) in terms of the scenario and even the look and feel of Eden and the fall of a supposed libertarian/freedom enclave under the sea into a supernatural fascist police state - and then it gets worse. The storyline at least is somewhat different from its thematic inspiration, so it doesn't feel like a complete retread.
In terms of gameplay the HOG scenes all play fine, and the puzzles were also pretty good - a reasonable mix and a moderate difficulty in most cases, and the point and click sections in between it all works well enough, nothing too illogical or jarring, and of course the HOG genre fits quite well into this semi-apocalyptic scenario of scavenging around for tools and clues as to what is happening. An alternative to playing the HOG scenes - dominos - is available, although it is pretty bland, and it seems a bit odd when these sorts of things are provided, as it seems unlikely there is big market of people that would play a HOG if the HOG scenes weren't there, as they tend to make pretty weak point and click puzzlers with this part taken away.
As has been mentioned in other reviews, one of the weaknesses here is the animations when characters are talking to you which makes them look like mannequins (although due to they story in a few cases this is somewhat appropriate), which is a bit jarring. Another minor issue is that the achievements are set up so you have to play the game twice - once doing only HOG scenes, once playing Dominos at each such scene, in order to get 100%.
However in summary this is a well made, if derivative, game that is easy to play, mildly challenging in places, and with an okay storyline and atmosphere.

It's painful to give a bad review, because I'm a dev myself. I want to like Starbound because I loved Terraria. Played 60 hours during early access, but came back today palyed for 1 hour and quit.
Controls in 1.0 is abysmal. It felt like they were trying to map a controller hotkeys onto a keyboard and mouse setup. The hotkey bar was labelled and they added "R" as a special hotkey for mining. I was constantly trying to hit "4" to switch to mining, then wondering why it didn't work. Many hotkey bars allows for a second slot (left and right click). Visually this is very confusing. My brain looking at the UI, expects the items to be mapped from 1-9, not 1 (left / right) 2 (left / right) etc.
There were a lot of other introductory pacing issues too. Enemies on the ground floor being too challenging behavior wise, paired with a flawed starting sword with a cooldown. But these are all secondary compared to the controls issue.
Please fix.

Starbound does a lot of things well, or at least acceptably well.  Unfortunately, it fails in one of the most basic and critical ways, which is providing good controls.
To be clear, when I say a lot of things, I don't mean everything but the controls.  There's a lot of other problems with this game - the very shallow pool that the procedural generation draws upon, the grind and repetition, and the fact that the game tries to both be a survival/building game and a classic platformer and fails to be really good at either.

PRECURSOR:
Fallout 4 falls into one of the latest genres releasing in todays age of Video Games.
Love it or Hate it.
Alot of people are upset about  Bethesdas business practices over the years. They were upset greatly when they released the Creation Club for thier paid mods. However, at the end of the day nobody is forcing you to purchase them.
And as far as people making claims that New Vegas was better than this.
The story was better, sure. Everything else was pretty awful.
I still hold the envroments and story of fallout 3 in a higher regard than either of these titles.
There is something way more interesting about exploring a blown out city than a desolate desert anyday.
THE REVIEW:
I've been a huge fan of Fallout since Fallout 3 and have played every game since then.
It even sparked my interest to check out some of the earlier Fallout games in the series.
Pros:
-Good Controls (Greatly mproved over other Bethesda RPGS)
-Large map to explore
-Weapon modabilty is a nice touch
-Nice Graphics
Cons:
-The Main Story is boring
-Player interations have very little weight
-No karma system
-Preston Garvey
BREAKDOWN:
-The story of Fallout 4 is not great by any stretch of the imagination. If you are playing Bethesda games only for the story, you're missing the point (that'd be like playing GTA for the story). There are much better subquests and side stories that really bring this world to life.
The return of "Survival Mode" (previously Hardcore mode) which was added into the game for FREE (post launch), encourages players to really see all the Commonwealth has to offer.
I have a feeling that the players that are complaining that the game has no good stories have never had to walk from Santuary to the Glowing sea.
The amount of travellers and encounters you can experience from walking to location to location is staggering.
For example, i once stumbled upon a group of survivors attending a funeral to a friend who had been killed during a raider attack. They had a preist and everything.
Things like this are missed when you Zip back and forth using Quick Travel.
-The Shooting game is strong in this one. Many guns feel and sound like they have power behind them. One of the earliest "Big Guns" you're given is a Minigun.
Using it against the run of the mill raiders literally mulches them.
Even the lowly pipe pistol feels real makeshift. The power behind a weapon like this wouldn't be fantastic. It feels like it was slammed together in a pinch.
These are just a few of my thoughts given my extensive time with the Game. Is it perfect? No.
Then again, very few games are these days.
If you can get 1 hour of gameplay for every $1 USD you spend on this, You've done well.
Seeing as i currently have over 10X that, i'd say i've done pretty great and would even still reccomend it.
Final Scores:
-Graphics: 8/10
-Sound: 9/10
-Story: 3/10
-Gameplay: 10/10
My Rating: 7.5/10

I would recommend this game to people looking for some fast-paced, zombie-killin' action that doesn't take itself too seriously.

Dementium II was a first person survival horror game on the Nintendo DS. I absolutely loved it, so I was excited upon hearing news of a HD PC port. This port however, turned out to be a disappointment. Poor, awkward controls (especially with the gun handling), and the choppy animations made combat dull while the cleaner "HD" graphics along just made the game look more cartoonish and took away the eerie atmosphere that the original had. There's also problems with graphic settings not saving, so you have to manually set that up every time you launch the game; not much of a problem of course, the game itself is relatively short, and the replay value is even lower than the original (it did not have a Survival mode the last time I played this port, and the original had one). Some achievements also don't work, so I advice achievement hunters to stray from this game.
Overall, I found it to be a poor experience (especially compared to the original NDS game). I wouldn't recommend it at the original price of 15$, nor the current price of 10$. I do think it is worth a try when you see this game up on a sale, but fans of the series should prepare themselves for disappointment.

With this relatively new trend of porting iOS and Android games to PC's it seems that small time portable developers have tried to push their way into this. Case in point: Nintendo DS games being ported to Windows PC's.
Don't assume this is going to be one of the few DS games to come to PC (there is Resident Evil Revelations after all). What you can safely think, however, is that the vast majority of these games are going to be♥♥♥♥♥♥
The reason why the DS is such a successful system is because it has a nice gimmick behind it, just like other modern Nintendo consoles. The gimmick here is that it has a touch screen that's relatively easy to use, and almost completley unheard of when the system originally came out. This is a challenging platformer with some of the best music I've heard in a game since things like 'Sword and Sworcery EP' and 'Fez'. The music itself as well as some of the visuals are quite reminiscent of 'Fez' although they are very different games.
When you first open the game, you are treated to the music straight away. There is no menu or text, other than the large '140' in the middle of the screen. Upon pressing any button you are thrust into the game itself, still with no instructions. This isn't a game for those new to the platforming genre, but those who have played the simplest flash game will easily be able to understand what to do.
Each level of the game has it's own music to match the obstacles present there. You will need the music on, as all the obstacles are synced up to the beat and mastering the rhythms can mean the difference between life and death. At the end of each level there is a boss, it will challenge the skills you have learnt through the level leading up to it. These bosses aren't the typical 'fights' you may be used to from other games, but I find them to be fairer and more challenging than most.
I absolutely adore the visual style of the game and the way it matches the music so well. The simplest touches can effect the game massively and when you first play it can be overwhelming, especially when you die. The patterns in the background that seemingly dance to the music fit the rest of the levels perfectly and aren't distracting or annoying, even when you are stuck on a particularly difficult section.
Overall this is one of the best platformers I have ever played, the controls are extremely responsive and I never felt like I died because it was the game's fault. For the price there is the perfect amount of content in my opinion. With just enough challenge and variety to give you a few hours of gameplay, and even more if you want all the achievements.
I would give '140' 5 stars, 10/10, 8/8 or whatever rating system you prefer, I love it. I will certainly be buying the soundtrack and I hope a sequel will be made one day. Great game!
EDIT: There's another level now and it's also great.

I'm not the sort to prejudice games over things like their being hidden object puzzlers; and the Artifex Mundi games are by far the best examples of the genre. Nonetheless A.M. has followed the method of if it isn't broke don't fix it, meaning they reuse their puzzles with cosmetic variations from one game to another. This has the unfortunate result that if you've played one of their games you've played them all.
That's O.K. if you think of the games as more visual novels with bonus puzzle content. Granted the writing isn't amazing; but it isn't bad either. I know I've yet to play an A.M. game I could make myself stop playing before the end. That's, on average, over 3 hours in one sitting. And, most of their games include a bonus chapter that extends gameplay another hour.
They do manage to do this without unnecessarily padding game length that overstays its welcome. I know that doesn't sound like much in an industry with triple AAA titles that boast hundred of hours of gameplay. But, for cheap casual games this is an achievement.
My recommendation, because of the "if you've played one you've played them all" problem, is pare your selections down to their better games. That would be Enigmatis 2 (but not the mediocre Enigmatis: the Ghosts of Maple Creek) as a top pick, Grim Legends 1 & 2 if you liked that, and the Nightmares from the Deep trilogy if you just can't get enough of these games.

"Abyss: The Wraiths of Eden" is pretty much your standard Artifex Mundi casual adventure Hidden Object Game (HOG).  The graphics are fairly nice, the story is trite but adequate, the voice acting is mostly tolerable, the puzzles enjoyable, and the Steam Achievements a bit irritating.  If you've played any Artifex Mundi HOGS, there's nothing unexpected.  Really, the only minor negatives are those Steam Achievements:  the HOG and the Dominoes Achievements are mutually exclusive.  So, to get 100% Achievements, you're forced to do two run-throughs.  And, as usual, since there are no saves, if you mess up, you have to finish that run-through regardless and then do it again.  One thing to point out with this game (like a lot of these HOGs) is that it's old enough that the user profile is not saved in the Steam folders or even in the standard Saved Games folder.  Instead, it's saved in the hidden folder [username]\AppData\Roaming\ArtifexMundi\Abyss_TheWraithsOfEden\CE.  So, if you're worried about losing it, make sure you back that up.
I got about 9.6 hours of good game play out of the game (6.5 hours for the first run-through with the Bonus Chapter and another 3.1 hours for the second run-through).  So, even at it's list price, the game is close to being worth it.  Of course, if you can find it on sale (as I did), then go ahead and snap it up.

As a tower defense game, this is one of the better ones out there. Unfortunately, this is the exact same version that you can play for free on android/ios or on various game websites. Don't get this game on Steam, go play it somewhere else, there is no added value here (unless achievements and trading cards are worth $10 to you). At least I got it as part of a bundle so I didn't have to pay full price for it. This is the reason I'm not recommending it, not because the game itself is necessarily that bad but more because this version is a grossly overpriced mobile port, not a real PC game.
As for the game itself, despite being one of the better tower defense games, it still has some issues. The biggest one being that this game frequently degenerates into a mad click-fest which I don't particularly like, for me I like tower defense games that give you some time to think and plan things out between waves and that give more flexibility in terms of tower placement. This game limits you to existing tower plots on the map, severely limiting what you can do with your towers.
These issues aren't even really inherent to a mobile game, bloons tower defense does a much better job in terms of tower variety, placement flexibility and planning between waves (even if the enemy types are boring).
Still, this game is a fun little time waster, but if you want a great PC tower defense game, go look at Orcs Must Die or Sanctum. They're cheaper and far better.

Bastion is an action game that has everything to be original and… fortunately, succeeds with flying colors!
The beautiful landscapes are a treat to behold.
The array of weapons at your disposal make it’s easy for you to destroy it in the most creative ways. (Hey, it’s not in the contract we have to respect public property). Jokes aside, they do let you come up with various strategies, which makes the game feel more dynamic.
The soundtrack is amazing, especially the tracks with vocals. (“Mother, I’m here” is amazing.)
Some climax scenes have great impact and work extremely well with the soundtrack chosen.
The Who Knows Where levels are pretty cool challenges and fill you in on the characters’ backstories.
It has good replay value. There are two possible endings and, if you get into the gameplay and the idols challenges, you will want to get all the achievements.
The narrator. Although I find it a very original and interesting way to tell a story, especially when he changes the dialogues depending on how well or not you do something or on your decisions making it feel like he’s actually watching your actions, may be annoying for some.
Despite the fact I have zero complaints about this, sometimes it feels to me that this choice of storytelling made it hard to interact with the various characters more, as it feels like the devs didn’t want to break the whole narration feel by attributing each of them their own voice actors.
Which leads me to…
There isn’t much interaction between you and the other characters. Because of the trips to Who Knows Where, you won’t find it hard to empathize with them as you’ll learn their stories, but I can’t help it but feel that a lot more could be done about them. Taking into account the context of the story, you’d expect the characters to be friendlier and connect a lot more with each other, which doesn’t happen because you can only talk with them when you find certain mementos. And I’m blaming the introduction of a narrator for this, as it’s his voice who speaks for the other characters, in the third person, which isn’t the best person to use when you want people to connect with the other characters.
Sometimes, you miss a lot of what the narrator is saying because many a times he talks when you’re busy trying not to get mobbed by 20 enemies at the same time, which is a shame. The narration is an important aspect of the game so it would’ve been better if they could time the dialogues to more idle moments so that you didn’t miss them.
The cursor. Even if you make your character face a certain enemy or object and attack, the attack won’t hit unless your cursor is also turned into that direction. Honestly, it’s not a big deal, but it is frustrating at times.
In conclusion, Bastion is an immersive, fantastic and, at times, surreal world that pays close attention to details and creative playing. I recommend it to everyone that likes fantasy settings and great storytelling.

Northgard is BIG room for growth, and I'm glad they're taking their time creating the storyline, Starcraft as you may or may not know has a huge amount of players who only play the game for the story, so hopefully Northgard's will be just as rich.

Highly addicitive, you're going to be staying up late when you're playing Northgard

Cons:
If your teamate leaves the game without transfering his land to you, you do not get it. This should be automatic.

When you are attacked randomly from NPCs, they do not leave the zone, instead, they randomly spawn. This reason I have an issue with this is it makes the world feel less alive, they SHOUlD leave one area to come to yours.

Where you put your buildings doesn't matter, again, this makes the world feel more alive. Putting the FIshermens hut closer to the fish SHOULD yeild greater resources.
____
All in all, despite Northgard's flaws it has amazing groth potential and is currently highly addicitive. Assuming the Devs adress some of the things I have listed, I foresee Northgard being big.

For example, what could be done is add duels as a in-menu thing, and then the duel can be hosted between the two players, rather than having both players connect to the same server. Then likewise, they can add a simple server file that only needs to start 1 instance of the server, and not 10 (or so the dev says 10.), which allows players to find and start p2p 16 player FFA matches easier.
I changed my recommendation to a negative for this very reason. I feel that is a game is entirely multiplayer, this should be the very first thing that gets done. Now, I have posted threads on the forums in an attempt to see if the devs would  change from this console-like method, but they seem adamant to keep their decision claiming UDK3 dosen't allow it (Which is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t, I've used UDK3 before and it does). The dev then goes to claim that in order for them to do this, they would need a commerical license, which is also not true. Adding on to this, don't expect to be able to find any multiplayer server  with a good ping, since the ones that are hosted always, are complete♥♥♥♥♥♥ The lack of players is for these reasons, and without players the game can't be played. So unless the devs change this multiplayer P2P method, I can't recommend this game.

I just finished the game after 14 hours of awesomeness and I enjoyed every single second I was playing.  Let me go over the things I enjoyed, ( Just about everything )
Story:
The story is just phenaminal.  While playing this game, the narrator is both telling and explaining the story and what has happened in the world.  The world becomes corrupted after the "Calamity" ends human life.  whats left is unstable platforms of ground that you explore looking for shards to repair the Bastion, the floating safehouse.  As you explore the world you find weapons that help further your cause, but ill get into those next.
Gameplay:
As you play the game, you find different weapons that can rearanged to suit your style.  For me, I liked using the Breaker Bow for long range, and then the Shotgun for aything that gets close.  The game takes youto several  places that were once thriving places in the old world, but are not only floating bridges and ruined structures.  As you progress, you learn about how and "what" caused this world to go to hell, and fight to return it back to its original state.
Music:
Man, the music in this game is really good.  Where ever you go there is music that helps set the tone of this new place that you are exploring.  All of it is beautifully done and really puts you into the mood.
Now all of this is fine and dandy, but dont be fooled, this is a really tough game if you are playing it for real.  There is a mode you can play, No Sweat Mode, that you have unlimited revives and cannot fail a level, but if you play the normal mode, you will have to restart, and it gets really tough later on if you havent upgraded your weapons enough.  you can also turn on Shrines, which increase the amound of XP and Moneyh you get, at the expence of tougher enemies.
This games is worth every penny, and there is a bit of replay value after beating the game.
Salute!
Edit:  So after completeing the game twice now, its left me in tears.  The ending is sad in the way that you have two options, and if you do one, you forget everything that has happened on this long journey and the friends you've made, and the other is to live out your days exploring with your new found companions in this broken world.  It makes you dig deep into your soul and chose how you want to proceed.  Amazing game Cannot stress enough,

Overview
Back in the days Sleeping Dogs should have been the counterpart to Grand Theft Auto.
Well Grand theft Auto is and will always remain a highlight. Especially in case of graphics, open world etc… but Sleeping Dogs confidents in his very own and special way.

You play an undercover police officer in Hong Kong, who tried to infiltrate the local triad. There you expect to collect tasks such as collect money, to fight other gangs, kidnap some important people, to steal cars etc. Soon you will experience that the Triad seek internal changes in the balance of their leadership.

At the same time you are giving important information to your boss police). You take out some enemies before you can hack some surveillance cameras. With these cams you can watch drugs handovers, viewing the dealer and call the police to arrest him. You can also do some special missions, following some member of the triade, make hidden photos and listen to some discussions about money transfers.

In my opinion, the story is very captivating and exciting. The voice acting is good and look very authentic. Dont forget, ist not america, ist hong kong, different driving sides, freakier cars and everything is like really densely built.

All quest are categorized in three different areas :

- Police Area (after completing a quest you earn xp and can level up)

- Triade Area (after completing a quest you earn xp and can level up)

- Social Area (after completing a quest you earn xp and can level up)

Many contents are comparable to Grand Theft Auto . There is a huge open world , lots of traffic , own cars (stealing, buying) , special clothing for your hero, weapons , several apartments and ancillary tasks. You can find hidden chests with money or clothing. To increase your energy, there are several shrines. To learn new fighting techniques, there are also hidden statues. These statues you can bring to your former teacher of martial arts. Afterwards he teaches you a new technique. You can train it in his fighting school. Focus of the game is the martial arts melee. Several kinds of enemies waiting for you :

- Light opponents

- Serious opponents

- Wrestler

- Enemies with weapons

- Covered Opponents

etc.


In addition to the main tasks that you can solve, there will be also little Quests to raise your Social Status. For example helping a woman to sink her car in the river. With those points you can buy better clothes. The clothes also allow you to earn some extra attributes (for example 5 % more damage on enemies in fights). After some time you will have enough money to buy anything, it just matters how is your current level in each area (police, triade, social). Some things you can only buy if you have a minimum level in one of the areas.


Graphics
I dont want to talk much about the graphics. Check out some screenshots, even if you dont play this game on ultra settings, it looks great. It can not exceed GTA, but it still looks good enough in my opinion.


Controls
You can play it with both controller or keyboard. I prefer Keyboard, somehow I play most of those kind of games with mouse and keyboard. At least its much easier for me to hit targets with weapons instead of using the controller.

My conclusion
If you like GTA, then you will like this for sure. You can feel the intensity of the main character. I really like his way he speaks, the way he acts. He fits totally for this job.

If you love martial arts fightings with a mix of grand theft auto flavour, an open world, undercover action, a great story, then go and get it. I can only recommend the game.

Enjoy it

Greetz
MajorKing

Ah well, this is a tough decision. I was baited by the good reviews and the nice looking previews, and as this game was in a bundle, I picked it up for the backlog. Time went by and I got to play it today - and I have to say, it would have definitely not been worth the full price of 8€.
But let's go deeper into it. The game is set in an interesting, haunted, underwater city. You play a woman that tries to find her lost husband, which - if you will - was an underwater-extreme-sport-archeologist-whatever-dude. And that's basically everything for pre-story. The game then throws you with a neat handdrawn cutscene right into it.
It then asks you whether you want to play a short tutorial, which is useless, and then you're on your own - depending on the difficulty you have chosen.
You'll have to do some "Where's Waldo"-style minigames or can alternatively do some kind of mahjongg-clone, then find some items around the scenes, and do a puzzle here and there. And here and there you'll find another little cutscene.
Storywise the game takes some time to build up and then develops a rather interesting story (which by the way could make for a great FPS à la Bioshock), which unfortunately then cuts off completly at about 95% and abruptly ends the game with a rather boring conclusion and a stupid teaser.
So now that we know about gameplay and story, what about graphics? While you can't expect much from a simple adventure game like this, it's actually drawn very nicely and has some decent detail to it. It is playable on 4:3 and 16:9, but will unfortunately stretch on 21:9. Also, if you have a 4k or QHD-display, you will notice that the game was created for much lower resolutions. But it's not that bad actually and should definitely not be a reason for not buying this.
On for the sound - it's good for the most part, environment sounds are nice, the soundtrack is decent but repeats somewhat to often, and then there's the synchronisation - while the synchro for other characters is ok, that for the player is actually really bad. It sounds like the voice artist went through an emotional drama whether or not she should actually continue voicing the game for the given paycheck. But hey, at least she doesn't talk that often, so that's nice*.
Now the last point - and this is the one why I would not recommend this game for 8€: It's just way to short. You can easily finish this in 3 hours and will probably squeeze no more than 4 hours out of it. Replay value is just not there since the story is completly linear and there's basically nothing you might miss while playing it.
But if this game is on a sale, you should absolutely grab it, if you're fine with casually playing a point and click adventure. If you're more into FPS like CoD, well, I don't even know why you have read this far.
* Note for feminists and/or anyone else who might feel insulted: This is not meant to be misogynistic but rather as a diss for the actually bad voicing itself. The statement would be the same if it was voiced by a male. Do with this as you will.

Game Menu Option: Two section – Volume and Miscellaneous settings. The volume section has the following: Music and Sound. The miscellaneous section has the following: Custom Cursor, Voice Overs, Difficulty Mode and Full Screen. Wide Screen is automatically supported in the game.
Game Difficulty Modes: Three game difficulty modes – Casual, Advanced and Expert.
Cinematic/Dialogues: All cinematic scenes can be skipped if you do not want to watch them. They can be watch over again under the cutscene section the extras.  There is an option for skipping the entire dialogue scene without having sit through it.
Voice Overs: Nothing much can be said about the voice overs asides from that they are well done.
Game Music/Sounds: Nothing much can be said about the music/sounds asides from that they fit well with the game without being intrusive.
Game Graphics: Nothing much can be said about the graphics asides from that they are nicely drawn with a painted feel to them.
Inventory Panel: There is no lock option for the inventory panel. However, it does slides up and down, whenever the mouse cursor hovers over it.
Notebook: Two sections – Notes and Objectives.
Map: The map interactive with useful indicators; map icons/markers. The legend on the map explains the function for each of the map icons.
Hidden Object Gameplay: Traditional word lists and Fragments items with some and/or no interaction required. Most of the hidden object scenes can be replayed in the hidden object section in the extras.
Domino Gameplay: This optional to play instead of looking for items in the hidden object scenes.
Puzzle Gameplay: Most of the puzzles are fairly easy to solve. Some puzzles has extra puzzles in them to solve. There is a skip button if the puzzle(s) becomes too tasking to solve.
Game Ending: There is an ending for the main portion of the game. The bonus chapter is the pre-sequel to the main portion of the game.
Game Achievements: In game and Steam. There are total of 20 different achievements to earn throughout the game. Each of the achievements has certain requirements before they’re obtained.
Game Bonus Chapter: This is only available after the main portion of the game is completed.
Game Concept Art/Wallpapers: 9 concept art and 8 wallpapers.
Game Soundtrack: 6 soundtracks from the game.
Game Length: There are eight chapters in the main portion of the game. The bonus chapter portion of the game mostly likely to have at least two chapters the most.
Game Trading Card/Badge: This a special feature only available in the Steam’s version of the game. The game drops three different trading cards only once and the rest of the cards: Community Market, Booster Packs and Trading. The game badge can be crafted after having all the card in the inventory then it can be upgraded four more times.

After 1.0 came out I got really excited to start playing this game again. To add some context I've been playing since maybe a month or two after the game came out as a beta. And in this time I've had a love/hate relationship with Starbound. When I first bought the game it had several bugs/glitches which were eventually fixed only to be replaced by more of them. Thats fine. Thats what beta testing is all about. So I would go on streaks of playing with or without friends (its fun either way but having a party is a whole new experience).
But really at this point I should be reviewing what I thought of 1.0 which is why i gave it a positive review for the game. There are a lot of bad reviews coming up complaining about how the game used to have so many bugs and such. note "used to" in my experience I encountered maybe 2 bugs. The story was well done and of decent length (It took me about 20 hours to complete). It also included several sidequests for the player to participate in if they chose to do so which helps with replayability a lot. There are some very good and enjoyable things that you can experience in this game so I'll put a pro/con list here for anyone still reading.
-Story is a good length
-Story is well told
-Several races to choose from with their own unique cultures/appearances
-Character customization
-Outfits
-Pets
-Near infinite number of planets to explore
-Lots of biomes to explore
-Boss fights were difficult but not impossible
-Lots of replayabilty value from side quests, colonies, upgrading, etc
-Nice graphics
-GREAT music
-Spooky moon ghosts
-Seems like there are plans to keep adding new content
-Lots of item variety
-Balance is off in the early stages of the game (enemies very hard to kill/deal a lot of dmg)
-Bug where you can get stuck in a block while building (Easily fixed by breaking it)
-Has some FPS issues in certain areas (On a well built PC)
-Upgrades are not very well explained
-Wiki can be unreliable from all of the previous builds (Not the dev's fault though)
-Combat is very boring early on in the game and stays mediocre into the end game
-EPP augments dont transfer with upgrades and are destroyed when a new one is applied
I hope this helps people who may be considering buying the game. In my opinion it is very worth your money. If you liked Terraria then you will like this game as well. Before I start the review I would like it known that I recently purchased the game in the summer sale and the following review reflects the £ 3.99 price tag I paid for it.
Overall I am quite pleased with my purchase.  I did play the original game (the main reason for this purchase) and as such this is a fairly good recreation of that game with a more modern and capable technology,   There are a number of interesting additions to the game, such as the ability to find new blueprints to improve you Walruses (tanks) and Mantas (aircraft).  The basic aim of the game is to take over as many of the 33 islands as you can and destroy the enemy carrier.  In that regard the game remains pretty much unchanged and has the original 3 island types (Defence, Resource and production).
The game does bring some new ways to fight to the table.  For example you can destroy an enemy’s dock and thus cut the island off from the supply chain while still leaving it under enemy control, but useless to them until the dock is repaired.  Also the Cruise missiles are a welcome addition to your arsenal.
Now we need to talk about the game's AI which is at best mediocre and in parts shocking.  The AI doesn't really offer a serious challenge to the player.  The main strategy the AI seems to adopt is more vehicles/defences = harder challenge.  On the surface this would be fine if the AI could actually fight reasonably well.  Even if you do lose a vehicle (if you are like me anyway) you know that you carrier has enough spares to just replace it.  Generally speaking a single player controlled vehicle can out match 5/6 enemy units.  When you also have your AI controlled allied vehicles in the mix only a serious miscalculation on your part means a bad ending for you.
I mentioned the AI controlled Allies above.  In total you can have 4 aircraft and 4 tanks assisting you.  This would be fine if the AI pathfinding for your vehicles was any good.  Unfortunately this is probably one of the biggest problems with the game.  While the Enemies tanks don't have a problem crossing a bridge your tanks do, your tanks constantly get stuck on the terrain, bump into each other and generally get stuck on a blade of grass.   You as a player then have to take over to get them "unstuck" and then hand the controls back over to the AI, only to have to do the same thing again 5 or 10 minutes later.   The aircraft are considerably better, but, even here there are problems such as occasionally not avoiding trees, radio masts and on one or two occasions the ground.
There are in dispersed with the normal type of gameplay some FPS missions.  Though in the grand scheme of things there are not that many when they do pop up I just feel bored with them.  Frankly the AI in these sections may as well just be saying lets line all the enemies up so you can shoot them for all the challenge they present.
The game ultimately is playable though somewhat frustrating at points.  It feels like an early access game rather than a released title.
If you feel that you can forgive the obvious flaws in the game then this is a worthy addition to your game collection assuming you buy it when it's on sale (Frankly at full price I would be a very unhappy bunny.

I went into this game with an unusual situation: i was panicking from a flu attack, and needed something to take my mind off it. this game, did just that, and way more.
There is just such a simple joy in floating in a grey void, swinging on dark grey platforms, as a red dot with an orange trail, all while flying through red bars, while relaxing music plays in the background. This game is just gentle. there is no other word for it. there is no way to fail, you can skip to the next level whenever you like (this is better than you think), and the music is sleep inducing to a point.
This game is one of the few real embodiments of minimalism in a video game. there is only one goal, there is only one track of music, and there is next to no colour, but all of this is only helps the game. however, even with such a simple game, the attention to detail is overwhelming. the next level is in the background, and the level even plays out as if you where there, the water has genuine reflection, and your glow will affect the colour of the blocks. The best part of the game in my opinion, is that
tailor it to yourself. there are settings that affect literally everything but the gravity, and core gameplay element (the swinging).
I owe this game a lot. it stoped my stress, and (technically) cured me of my flu (by making me forget i was even sick).
Thank you Floating Point. i had no expectations of you, but you blew them out of your dark grey water none-the-less.

To be honest, if you think I would suggest this one, you're RIGHT ON TARGET; because that's correct! It's a simple mini-game based point & click adventure game, where each of the levels has 6 scenes, where in each one, you have to figure out within at least 15 seconds, to figure out how to disarm the bomb. (And sometimes, figure out WHERE THE BOMB EVEN IS!)
This game is a comedic game; nothing dirty, but rather AWKWARD; the main character is in fact, "McPixel"; a parody of two characters, named MacGyver, and his other parody character, named MacGruber. Each episode is simple; YOU HAVE TO STOP THE BOMB! (Or whatever disaster will happen.) Note that the main hero is not a very smart fellow, so you play as him, (and if lucky) figutre out how to stop a disaster from happening.
So, what makes this game so awesome?!? Dude; this game is so dang awkward, that it's funny! If you like a good laugh, and like good, simple "point & click adventure" style puzzle-based gameplay, (that will usually take at least a minute or two, just to solve the puzzles) this game is 100% guaranteed, for a good laugh! Among games that are categorized as "SteamPlay" games, all DLC for this game is FREE!
Don't forget; ANYONE can even make their own levels, with the downloadable level editor, too; the official website has a tutorial page that will teach you how it works, because it doesn't require any professional programming knowledge; at least according to what it looks like, of course!

The game itself is pretty short and simple, but what makes this game truly great is the voice acting. The narrator does an amazing job of telling a dark and brooding story that really sets the tone. Other games should be looking to this one to see how it should be done. Pick it up on sale, and give it a whirl.

Town of Salem is an interesting concept held down by an absolutely dire community.
At around $5 or free as a browser game, this game is extremely cheap entertainment, and I'd definitely say that's the main appeal to it, anyone can play at any price (Steam version gets you some extra bonuses) Also there's a DLC for $5 too.
It'll work on pretty much any PC, it obviously works perfectly on my 7700k + 1070 rig, but it also works exceedingly well on my i7 5700HQ with integrated graphics. So a plus for that. Just make sure your processor and RAM are semi decent.
It's a great game to play with friends, providing you don't give too much away. Although if you're all town, it's fun to work together to catch out Mafia and Serial Killers, so a plus for that. It's a game that requires either great teamwork, or deception.
There's a ton of roles and every scenario plays out differently, rarely will games play out the same way, plus as you have a vastly different role every time (No two roles are really close) It makes it very interesting.
It's easy to spend a few hours on this game (matches only last about 20 minutes or so) but even solo, it's quite easy to chill out on, you can also use your other screen easily while still watching when you die.
Community is absolutely awful, whether it's just being toxic, or a Lookout absolutely screaming that someone's Godfather because you've just watched him visit and kill 3 people (and then he kills you and wins the game) The community can be especially dumb at times and refuse to lynch people despite the evidence being blatantly obvious. Or you can be me and get killed by a Vigilante on the first night when I'm a Medium (killing two town essentially) There's definitely a lot of toxic players who just report you for anything too.
: I'm not gonna complain too much about this, let's just say it has mobile game style microtransactions in a Steam game, that's pretty much it.
It's a good game that's cheap and cheerful, it's a good game for some banter with friends, but it's definitely absolutely tugged down by the community at times, do not underestimate how bad the community can be, trust me. Although there's no real cons except that.

Imagine a John Woo Grand Theft Auto. That's what we have been blessed with by Sqaure Enix in Sleeping Dogs. Parkour (free running), fist-i-cuffs fighting a la Batman series, and cover system based shotting gameplay with Max Payne esque bullet time. The gameplay itself is top notch. The only bug I encountered was a car was halfway stuck in the ground and the vehicle just behind was attempting to drive over it and eventually caused enough damage to blow them both up. As for the parkour, which is a massive part of the game from chasing missions to collecting hidden lockboxes, is fairly smooth. The only issue I have with it is the fact the not everything is climbable. It will throw you off many times. The story is pretty damn good and holds its own. A hint of The Departed is present. The undercover cop rises through the ranks and ends up becoming "too attached or too involved" in the gang. There are a couple of predictable twists, but still a very involving story with some very deep and graphic cutscenes. I honestly did not expect myself to enjoy this game so much. My non-professional opinion? 9/10. Definitely recommended.

This HD version of Dementium 2 is the PC port of a 4-year old Nintendo DS game. That said you can immediately notice the graphics that are not on par with today's PC standards. Also, the gameplay is simple, the controls are a bit non-responsive and the story is not exactly long. You can complete William's story in a mere 3 hours.
Still, Dementium 2 can be fun. It is a horror FPS game and you have all the weapons you need in such a game (knife, flamethrower) along with all the monstrosities you expect to jump at you at every corner. During the gameplay you proceed from room to room annihilating mentioned monstrosities while occasionally picking up an object only to use it elsewhere to overcome an obstacle.
I like how the game transitions you sometimes - while half of it takes place in a mental institution and in its surrounding village and caves the other half puts you in the same areas but in a hellish, underworld-like environment. One could call it a day and night cycle that is often repeated.
Dementium is mediocre at best but a good pastime. If you have nothing on your plate and do not desire to pick your next AAA game up you can have fun with it. Its low price can also get you closer to making this decision.

Technical difficulty solutions first, game review second.
Let me begin by saying I had problems running this game on windows 7. It continually crashed upon starting until I went into the computer folder for this game, checked properties, & found it was 'set' to run on windows XP, changed that to windows 7 & now game starts fine.
Another problem that needs fixing every time you start the game is video resolution from options menu. I set mine to 1280x720 because it fits screen, be mindful that certain resolutions cut out images/text, you know your res is right when you can read the full text [Reset to Default] instead of seeing [et to Defa].
Last problem before I address gameplay, playing in fullscreen, it works great in-game after turning it on...until you turn game off & return to play later -it goes back to windowed mode. Go to options, you'll find fullscreen mode IS SELECTED & the [Apply] button is not visible, don't panic. Change the resolution in order to make the [Apply] button appear & set fullscreen, then change res to reapply desired res.
Review:
Gameplay:4/10
Controls:9/10
Visual:5/10
Audio:8/10
Gameplay: I own 'Dementium: The Ward' for DS from which this game is a sequel. That said, the enemies are similar & equally aggressive for your blood, they will lock you in rooms at times and force you to fight wave after wave until victory or death. Half of the puzzles you have to find clues to solve, the other half are too easy. The game is also very short compared to the DS version.
Controls: They made the controls very proper for a FPS, hotkeys for all your weapons, looking at map pauses game, you can remap the keys to your liking. Only thing i didn't like was the lack of hotkey for health items.
Visual: I rated this low because the game has HD in it's name & the only times this quality ever occurs is during cutscenes. Otherwise the game has a creepy appearance of sanity twisting, blood covered iron in between lucid moments of roaming a prison for the criminally insane. Aside from that, if an enemy is visually reeling from a bullet you just put into it & you shoot it again, it will occasionally pass through to the wall.
Audio: I enjoyed the music and sound effects as they are straight out of the DS version I know so well. The worms still squeel, the bonesaw still has that satifying grate, & the dissembodied heads still scream in anguish just like they always do. That said, the main character never speaks, & the main villian never shows any emotion after revealing his true colors. Sad really, I wanted to hear his triumph, his fustration, his fear...or at least throw me a maniacle laugh, SOMETHING!
I would recommend this game if you like horror shooting games & catch it on sale like I did, or if you've played Dementium: The Ward (not required to enjoy though)

If like me you've played Dementium II on the Nintendo DS a few years back and liked it, be advised: this is EXACTLY the same game and same feel you'll get playing this HD version on PC. Although graphics are not that good by today's standards (polygons count is low and textures are a bit bland), I assume they may have been left ''simple'' on purpose, as to not stray too far from the DS version yet feel more polished. Controls are floaty and hit detection is not perfect (although ennemies will turn red to indicate they're taking damages). Difference between walking and running is hard to notice but is nonetheless needed at some points in the game. In the end, since I haven't finished the game at the time, I'm glad I picked it up on sale for $ 1.00. Would not have paid 10 bucks for it. Also, french being my primary language, I can't say I was too impressed with the translation, so I can imagine other languages included in the game must have typos or syntax errors as well.
BUY IF:
-you liked the DS version and want to experience it again on a bigger screen with higher def and better textures.
-it's on sale for $ 5.00 or less (as a bonus....piece of advice...)
DON'T BUY IF:
-you expect a rehashed version of the game with crisp graphics and revamped gameplay
-you never played a DS game in your life and hope this game is a worthy contender in the FPS horror genre (the first F.E.A.R game does a better job at it and cost around the same.)

One of the best tower defence games i've played.
Charming graphics, funny speech and sounds, very strategic. You build towers in preset locations using money, which you get by killing enemies. While battling, you upgrade said towers again using money. After every succesful battle you are awarded up to three stars each mission, which you use to unlock perks for your towers and these perks are well thought out, offering many gamechanging mechanics and -ofcourse- more damage.
All towers are equally useful: magic for strong/armored enemies, bombs for crowds, archers for small & fast enemies, soldiers for stoping & gathering enemies. You also have 2 special powers which have a cooldown and can be used indefinately (1.inserting 2  soldiers anywhere you want and 2. meteor shower). By the way, special powers get perks too.
And then there are "heroes", which are directly controled by the player, have special powers and suit many different playstyles (strong melee, weak magic, ranged, teleporting among others). Between heroes, special powers and the fact that you can demolish your own towers (and get a little refund) to build a different towers in their place, you will never feel powerless or blame the game.
Make no mistake though, the game becomes gradually challenging. You won't be needing lightning reflexes, but you'll have to learn by trial and error sometimes. If you are easily frustrated, there's always the "casual" difficulty setting.
As for longevity, this game is a completionist's dream. Beat the main campaign and you still have 2 challenges for each mission (which restrict what types of units and level of upgrades you can use - for me these were even more fun than the main mission!) and a couple random missions poping up all over the map. I haven't completed everything yet, but i'd say you're getting at least 20 hours of fun.
Well worth the price.

is one of the best fighting games I have played to date.
**PROS**

(as well as a great tutorial). Fast paced action with easy combo executions will keep you and your enemy constantly on guard; you will very rarely be in a neutral position waiting for your opponent to make a move. This is easily one of my most enjoyed fighting experiences (I'm from a background of Smash Brothers, Street Fighter and some other 2D fighters)
-
. Easy to follow for people new to the series with a decent amount of "WHAT!?!?!?!" moments.
-
Yes, you can tag team!! Why don't more  games have this feature?? Simply put, you get to pick 2 players to fight against 2 other players in the SAME MATCH (this can even be done with a friend playing the second character on your team, just get another controller for them.)
-
within the game ranging from alternative character costumes to  galleries of the fighters, stages and music. It will keep you busy for a while to try to collect enough coins to unlock  everything.
-
While some of the mini-games are dull...such as Test your Might and Test your Strike (pretty much just button mashing) other ones like Test your Sight and Test your Luck are pretty fun to mess around with (One being a simple sight game to see if you can keep track of a fast object, while the other gives normal matches special events that make the game play more unique example.... Headless combat or infinite super meter). There is also a "Challenge Tower" with 300 different combat scenarios for you to beat (some..more fair than others.)
**CONS**
-
. If you're new to fighter games, you'll have a lot of frustrating moments with this one (Especially in story mode). As the story progresses, you'll switch between different characters in order to suit that section of the story, this will force you to learn a new string of combos or new special skills for that particular character, this does NOT help you when you're suddenly having to fight 1 v 2 battles or the bosses. The bosses are especially brutal if you don't know their attack pattern or simply have no idea what you're doing in general; they have insane damage increase, health increase, and worst of all armor which prevents flinching <-- something you need for combos. To me it felt like the only way to beat this game sometimes was to use cheap tactics.."Okay you're going to use cheap moves? Fine I'll just do the same". Just be prepared for some frustrating matches. The best advice I can give is to use throws as much as you can.
-

Why the hell are they going to make a story mode that's about 5-7 hours of gameplay and yet make it impossible to choose where in story you can play ( even AFTER you have beaten it)??? Nope, they have you start from the beginning, and if you have already started the story and you wish to play an earlier section you must beat the entire thing to restart it...................

The only way you can fight solo is through the ladder matches, but even then..you can't even choose which opponent you get to fight against, it's all random. (You can also use the training mode, but you can't even execute fatalities there.)
-
Why is there no love for the offline single player experience? The only way to play some of these fun modes in solo play (like headless combat or zombie mode) is though the "Test Your Luck" game mode...but again...this is all RANDOMLY SELECTED. You simply press the start button and a roulette picks them for you; you might end up with something you like..for example Infinite meter...but then you also end up with bleed effect...LAME. The roulette should have been a variation of a custom match, not the actual custom match. The only other way to trigger the special events is if you have a two player match where the 2nd player inputs a code on the loading screen along with you...and that will still sadly only give you ONE special event, nothing else. Potential wasted :(

First i want to say that i want to like this game! I love RTS games and havent found one in quite some time thats worth paying for sadly i dont think this is it either. This game has SO MUCH potential but until that time theres tway to many things i didnt like about it.
My main problems are as follows:
- Unreal building limit in an area you control (average is 3 per area) : theres just not enough structures as there is a max to the amount of workers for that building, which is 2!!!! those two things coupled together makes resourse gathering impossible to keep up with what you need.
- Fighting unit count is unreasonably low especially when compared to AI population: my max army was 8 people and a war chief as there was not enough land or resources to house more.
- Resource production/management almost impossible: There is set areas to make a farm areas that are very few in the WHOLE map that a staggering 2 villagers can work and only 1 fishing hut per water with fish making keeping up with food especially as you try and feed your 10 warriors a constant uphill battle not to mention when winter comes and a blizzard ravages your supplies. The lack of food and even gold generating sources makes it even more difficult to advance than it should be.
- Ridiculously finite amount of resorces you DESPERATELY NEED (stone and iron): i have literally found 2 sources of stone which every single building needs at least 10 of to upgrade. 1 stone pile supplies 20 stone, then a perk to get 30% increase mining and a one time choice of another perk that gives you a small supply. i was literally unable to finish a conquest as i could not upgrade my scout hut so he could discover the area the enemy was at because i had no stone.
- Fixed rate that colony size increases and NOTHING you can do to get villagers faster(one town hall upgrade for no noticeable difference): if you get raided and lose too many villagers your game is over. the rate you can get new ones is painfully slow then add in the cost to promote a villager to a military unit its not gonna end well.
The AI has a what i have to call a infinite resource pool as i killed who knows how many warriors but also a war bear at least 12 times and what id assume is their war chief more times than that. Those 2 units are extremely expensive and everytime they had new units there was 6 - 10 of them which is impossible numbers to have after losing all their units to my small army and also considering the unit cap as well. Again i want to like this game so badly but theres som much wrong with it the difficulty lever (nothing worng with a gme being hard but this is on a new level), resourse management, NO resources, AI not bound by same lrules  the player is and the restrictive aspect of evvery single part of this game kills it. Hopefully theres a complete turn around by the time its released.

It's a great game; worth picking up if you are looking for a real time strategy game that is simple to learn yet has variability and tactical control to keep you coming back for a casual game or two a few weeks later.
Play takes plase on a large island where you claim territory to secure various paths to victory (research, economic, fame, or elmination). Territories are procedurally generated and shroaded in fog of war so you need to explore, than pick the best territories to claim adjacent to your starting territory.
Your Vikings spawn based on a number of factors (food, happiness, available housing) and you can assign them to jobs for resource collection or defense. To assign a job, you must have built the corresponding structure and there must be worker slots available. You can change jobs anytime. Each territory you have acquired can house 2-4 structures and some have special resources like fish or iron mines. Grabbing the right territory and constructing the right buildings based on your victory strategy is key to this game.
Games last half hour to an hour depending on size and skill of the competition. AI is a competent opponent and tends to attack you where you are vulnerable. Some clans prefer one victory strategy, but you are largely at the mercy of the game board; one of the best part of the game is there is no one-strategy-always-wins. Once you figure out what your opponants are doing, you may need to switch strategies . Balancing territory/resource acquisition with your ability to defend it is key.
The game suffers from the same paradox as settlers of catan: if you pull out too far in front of your competition, everyone will gang up on you. So picking a victory condition goal isn't enough, you have to make sure you can protect your ability to secure that goal.
Simple to learn, hard to master; very replayable. Recommend if you like RTS, City builders, and strategy board games.

Aliens vs. Predator is a game that offers you 3 campaigns each following a different character through a derivative narrative.
The Marine campaign gives you a shallow first person shooter putting you in the shoes of a rookie marine whom has crossed far too many black cats in his life.
The Alien campaign gives you an interesting stealth adventure as an Xenomorph that managed to show some character and became the Teachers pet.
The Predator campaign gives you a unique stealth/melee combat experience very reminiscent of the original movie.
Or atleast on paper you do, in reality you get to experience one campaign through the eyes of a Marine an Xenomorph and the Predator. You traverse through the same levels time and time again making the game feel very slow at times.The game will constantly hold your through the marine campaigns and it is very linear but some of the Predator and Alien levels really open up and let you tackle the levels in a few different ways.
The Ai in this game varies from good to bad. Sometimes the Xenomorphs will run along the walls and sneak up behind you making the game incredibly tense and atmospheric, Other times the Marine and Synth Ai will have Stormtrooper aim. This is even more prevelant in the Predator campaign, you are either constantly locked into a 1v1 melee battle with an Xenomorph or you are just stabbing it in the♥♥♥♥♥♥over and over while it runs away.
I would say overall the Ai was decent but flawed in some aspects.
The Campaign I enjoyed the most was absolutely the Predator one, it felt very unique and fresh to play. The only problem was a distinct lack of weapons to choose from, you get 4 weapons in total that would become available to you as you progressed and the standard melee attack. The game could have been so much better if they had chosen to add more weapons and gadgets to the Predators arsenal, It would have added much more needed depth and replayability. The Predator campaign had some terrible pacing issues, Towards the second half after a boss battle the game gives you his 4th weapon the combistick. This weapon allows you to one shot any Synthetic, Marine or Alien. This removes any need for Stealth or tactics and felt totally overpowered.
The Marine campaign is the most mediocre of the bunch. Shooting the Xenomoprhs was satisfying but there wasnt much of a variety in weapons to choose from. It followed a strict formula of Run here, Shoot this, Cutscene the entire way through and felt incredibly repetitive and lackluster although it did definitely have its moments reminiscent of the Aliens movie. The Combat Synthetics you face are an absolute bore to fight, simply put they are just bullet sponges.
The Alien campaign was the most flawed of them all. The only options it gave you to kill were luring somebody over, Sneaking up on them and grabbing them for a one shot kill, Or just beating them to death with light and heavy melee attacks. It also featured a harvesting system which was the most poorly executed aspect. Sneaking up behind a civillian allows you to trigger an animation that holds them down letting a facehugger jump on there face, This was cool to do the first time but it reaps no benefit in game and has only 2 animations.
The game was not very hard to beat, Even playing on Hard difficulty most of the game was a total cakewalk. The game will hold your hand through the entirety of all 3 campaigns. I played all 3 campaigns in about 7 hours, the Marine campaign taking 3, the Predator another 3 and the Alien campaign being 1 hour long. Boss battles can range from a 5 minute slow grind to a 10 second sprint, Each providing no real challenge.
For £10 I can hardly complain though, The game may be flawed in many aspects but it still offers you 3 Distinct playstyles, Great visuals and gory animations and Multiplayer with a bunch of maps.
Final Score: 5.5/10 Nuke the site from orbit.

I only recommend this game if you get it at a pretty significant discount, and even then it's a maybe (more at the end).  It's like GTA meets the Batman series of games.  Combat is, for the most part, super easy.  Occasionally there are frustrating moments where you are suddenly in a quick-time action sequence but there is no really clue what is happening.  This won't kill you, but it's annoying when you get thrown because you thought you would have to right-click when you were supposed to mash F.
The camera is alright for most of the game, but can be really frustrating when you're driving and need to reverse at all.
I'd recommend a controller for this game.  I played with mouse & keyboard even though I have a controller, but there are moments when you can tell this was definitely made with a controller in mind.  This is especially true in some of the DLC -- in the DZS-90 quests in the Wheels of Fury dlc, you have to drive your car using WASD while simultaneously holding down Q periodically to charge the car's EMP pulse.  It was really frustrating.
The story-line was pretty good, but it felt like everything was on rails.  Since the main character is an undercover officer, it would have been nice to be given the choice between siding with the law and siding with the Triads.  On the other hand, the ending seems ripe for a sequel.
Also, some of the game-play was just repetitive.  A lot of police missions are simply going to a location, beating up some bad guys, hacking a nearby camera, then returning home to use the camera to identify a drug dealer and send the police to arrest him.  After the second time, it's just boring and the only reason to do it is for in-game objectives rather than because it's also fun.
There are lots of races, but they are a little frustrating too.  Vehicles are categorized by class, and a race only allows certain classes of vehicles.  But there doesn't seem to be a good way to tell which class vehicle a race is before-hand, and all vehicles within a class are not created equal.  Speaking of -- the driving is sometimes very frustrating, and unfortunately there's LOTS of it.  I started looking for cabs because I was tired of spending a couple minutes driving across town just to trigger an event that sends me driving back across town again.  And don't you know it, it seems there's never a cab around when you want one!
My caveat for purchasing this game w/ the dlc:  Apparently you get a LOT of experience with some of the DLC.  I was maybe 30 minutes to an hour into the game and had already gotten level 8 in both police and triad.  The maximum level for each is 10.  You can simply opt out of using a lot of the dlc outfits, costumes, and vehicles but you can't opt out of that experience I don't think.
Anyway, I started ignoring achievements and cop missions (since I hit level 10 so fast), but I logged around 15 hours of play in this game before beating it.  (A few times I left the game paused while I ran an errand or folded laundry.)  Game was fun while it lasted but definitely had the potential to be more than it was.

Dementium II HD is a PC port of a DS game of the same name, just without the whole HD thing, it claims to be a survival horror game and it succeeds in the horror part by being a clunky horrific mess of a game with very few redeeming qualities, but I am getting ahead of myself.
In Dementium II you play as William Redmoor, who has been locked up in an insane asylum presumably after the events of the first game, the game starts with you entering a nightmare world that looks like the offspring of Hellrazor and Silent Hill, and I will admit some of the designs of enemies and architecture are very well done and creepy.
Soon you meet a doctor who tells you about how they let out something from your mind and he's very sorry in the real world but in the nightmare world he's some insane man who keeps throwing monsters at you or... something... this brings up a major pain of the game's story, if you never played the first Dementium, and lets face it, you haven't, you will have no idea what is going on, why everything is like how it is, and who these people are, nothing is ever explained and even if you did play the first one I doubt the plot of this game would make any sense at all.
Combat is clunky at best, being a port of a DS game you can guess the controls feel weird, they are unresponsive at times and guns just seem to fire oddly, the gun sight is a little off to the right and moves with the gun, which I suppose is not really a negative given that most survival horror games have really bad combat anyway, but it also is not a problem because by the time the more powerful monsters came around I already had twenty or so healing pills, and this was on normal.
Quick side note on the sound design, it is really bad, enemies make the same sounds over and over, annoying chains clanking together or the odd skittering sound or better yet the very poorly done laughing sound the skulls make, and on top of that you will hear the same music for combat every... single... time... and it is really, really bad.
Overall this game took me about three hours to beat on normal and got all the achievements along the way, so is it worth it? No not really, the game is short, easy despite being clunky and a bit buggy, the plot makes no sense, dispite being 'HD' you can still tell it was a DS game, and even if some of the monster designs are alright you could just play one of the Silent Hill games and get the same effects wrapped in a much better package.
I never played Dementium II on the Nintendo DS where it was originally released, but after beating this version I looked up videos of it and that seems like a much better game... doesn't look amazing or anything, but better then this, and worth pointing out the original developers of this game did not make the PC port.

This game is a zombie survival title requiring you to remain in your team of four in order to increase your chances of survival. This game doesn't have quick save so you have to be on your guard the whole time. It can get frustrating near the last level of each campaign where you have to fight off waves of zombie hoards and tank monsters. There are some cheap moments where a tank monster will instantly punish you with zero health then having to restart the level (remember there are no checkpoints) so this game is not without its flaws. There are also a few raging moments where there would coincidently be a witch, hunter and smoker for example and then you get gang♥♥♥♥♥♥♥from all directions. The difficultly can be a sudden spike up in some cases if you are new to this game on even normal difficulty. There is also a very limited arsenal of weapons like the sniper rifle, m16a2, colt 45, Uzi, pump action shotgun, and auto shotty, pipe bomb and molotov cocktail. If you can tolerate some of these flaws, then this game is worth checking out.
