Town of Salem is a ton of fun, especially with friends.
In Town of Salem you get assigned a role and join a town of, usually, 14 others. There are a huge variety of roles! And even more will be added with an upcoming expansion that looks really promising! These roles are (but not limited to): Mayor, Medium, Investigator, Escort, Consigliere, Amnesiac, Godfather, Executioner, Jester, Serial Killer, and so on. Based on your role you have a distinct goal. The Mafia are supposed to work together to kill all who oppose, the serial killer must finish EVERYONE, and the town must survive to see the end of all evildoers and killers, etc.
What's amazing is that despite the fact that there are some 30 roles or so, almost every role feels very distinct and has a unique playstyle (apart from escort/consort which I think are the most boring roles in the game). So one thing Town of Salem does very well is that it makes the gameplay always unique. This is true because there are so many distinct roles, but also because NO GAME of Town of Salem ever plays out the same way.
The constant wondering of who is who and whether or not you can trust those who stand to your left and right create such tension that the game is almost always exciting. Even in death you can still possibly affect the outcome by communicating with the medium. In my opinion, this is Town of Salem's greatest strength.
Town of Salem also does freemium gaming right (for the most part). There are two types of in-game currencies. One can only be purchased with real world $$$, and the other is earned after each match. Almost all items can be purchased with the in-game currency. There are only a select few which can only be purchased with real $$$, and they are all cosmetic. The only items which aren't purely cosmetic are "Scrolls" and they simply increase the likelihood you get to play a certain role over another.
Despite all these positives though, there are some negatives..
Young playerbase
The playerbase APPEARS (I'm not sure of this) to be quite young, and some of the logic of the players seems lacking sometimes. However, there are different game modes and by gravitating more towards ranked play you can avoid those who are just goofing off.
Night 1
Night 1 honestly sucks because it's very possible to die night 1 and there are many roles in which, if you die the first night or any of the early nights, your presence is essentially useless and the rest of the game is a snorefest. Nightmares about getting killed on night 1 more have honestly woken me up in the middle of the night lol.
Random Lynchings
This is somewhat tied to the first complaint, but in normal matches and even in ranked play sometimes, townies will randomly lynch people without much rhyme or reason. It's pretty frustrating if you play a critical role and your town randomly lynches you and greatly hurts your chance of victory, or even more frustrating if they somehow make a rally smart choice and you were the serial killer, mafia, executioner, etc.
High(ish) learning curve
There are A TON of abbreviations players use in the game to make communication fast and effective, since you only have so much time to talk each day. So, for new players, learning all the abbreviations and initialisms can be quite tiring and take a while. I have 10 hours at the same of this review though and by now I am pretty comfortable with all abbreviations, though. So it's not too bad.
These, relatively tiny, complaints aside though, Town of Salem is a great game and honesly has provided me with a very fun and never old casual gaming experience. It has brought an even better version to a classic game which I LOVED to play with my friends at gettogethers when I was younger.
One final note: You may be thinking "Why do I buy this game on Steam? It's a free broswer game!". That's true. However, one thing to consider is that the new expansion will come out soon, and it will be $10 online, and only $5 if you buy this version on Steam, so either way everyone will have spent $10 altogether. In addition, the game awards currency to be used on cosmetic upgrades for your character. If yoy buy the Steam version you get 100% more in-game currency after every completed match. It's a really nice bonus.
All in all, you should get this game. It's fun, it never gets old, the roles are unique, a new expansion is coming, the profanity filter is actually hilarious, and the game is very casual. It's a great fit for almost any type of gamer, because this is a classic we all used to love playing with our friends, made a lot more accesible and easier.

[tl;dr]
If there's one game I would highly recommend against, it's this; Tanki Online. Just don't... It's free entry, but it's not a free game; if you want to see a game that is really badly reliant on micro-transactions, where power leveling through in-game purchases is going to give those who pay a huge advantage, while the rest grind and get breadcrumbs, don't play this game!
I have been playing this game for over 5 years, last time I played it was a year or two ago (off-steam), but the bottom line is that you should never trust the company Alternativa Platform. They will screw you over and you won't notice it until it's too late, and both their fanbases and their moderator staff team have a huge bias of positivity towards the company, to a point where you will get into trouble for squaking the wheel even if you're not actually breaking any of their own rules. Don't play their games, don't talk to them, don't even give them a chance. They are ♥♥♥♥ed in the head, as are their games; this one (Tanki Online) and TX, and especially this one!
[Gameplay]
The gist of the game is simple; play as a tank in third person perspective with a combo of a weapon and hull that "suits" you in various matches and maps to win. A tank shooter, basically. It's quite fun for a while, but then you start to realise that a lot of things are off...
It's a lot of grind, to get crystals (in-game currency), but even when you try to do so, you will be out-powered by players who have higher upgrades than you just because they paid a lot of cash (I paid, regrettably, at least $200 for this♥♥♥♥♥♥ and I still haven't got most of the core good stuff). In the past, you could pay no more than $100 in the game and you would be fine, paying through $10 increments (except if you were purchasing through your phone, which was and still is way more goddamn expensive for less), or even nothing, you'd still feel satisfied and actually had a chance to purchase good upgrades without paying much of anything. Now it's the same♥♥♥♥♥♥essentially, but much more expensive. The total garage price trippled ever since the update "Rebalance", and has been getting more and more expensive over time.
[System]
At first you probably won't find the game so bad, but when the time comes where you need to upgrade your weaponry for up to M1, or at the very least M2, you will realise you're ♥♥♥♥ed. The game also relies on supplies, and while there have been tweaks to make them less expendable and easier to deal with by those who don't use them, if you were to use them, you could never reliably purchase them without paying for in-game currency. One supply costs at least 50 crystals, ~15 if you purchase a discount pack of -70% or something, although that's like 1000 of each supply, something you will need to grind for regardless to purchase and even then is unreliable, and equates to a loss, as you won't get more crystals from using them. It'll be a waste if if you use a supply up and die soon after without killing any other opponent. And fighting opponents who too use supplies regularly means someone's gonna end up having wasted their crystals. Could it be... everyone?
There are some really cool weapons and hulls in the game, honestly, the thought to combine them, I have never seen this idea anywhere before. But while it's fun for a while, the way the game is balanced, and this was commented by a staff member, saying something along the lines of "the idea is for you to be able to afford one hull and one weapon, fully upgraded by the time you reach the last rank". Now, imagine Overwatch, or any MMO shooter game, where, once you get to a higher skill level/upgrade level you can only use one player. Nothing else, just one player. And you'll need to either grind a year to fully upgrade another.
Oh, and they have loot boxes now as well! When did those come in, I don't even remember...
[Balance]
Weapons? My god, no... The long and mid-far range weapons are way more effective at almost any ranges, so, selecting a close range weapon isn't killing enemies quickly with the thread of being killed, it's more like a suicide mission. Mid-range or "short" range weapons (those being mainly the plasma ones). If there's one weapon that is the weakest of them all ever since the good ol' "Rebalance" update, it's Ricochet.
Hulls, unless they have changed the game to have a similar mechanic, they seemed alright to me, just so long as you can keep up the upgrades to your ranking level!
[Graphics]
This will probably run on a lower computer. Their old graphics had a style to them, the new ones are just a good-graphics wanabe, resulting in a relatively ugly baby of roblox graphics and of a some-what realistic shooter. That's the best I can really describe this as. It's for rendering reasons, really.
[Game Design]
Map design makes absolutely no sense. Though, it's limited assets, with a tiled system in place, so it's kind of no wonder. There is a plethora of maps, but you'll more often than not be playing in a few of them because popularity, and in-game systems beat diversity every time. If I remember correctly, you can't select a map without making a "pro" battle anymore, so, if you want to complete your missions, you'll need to grind in a few maps for months on end, it'll become your second day-job essentially.
[Community]
If I didn't make myself clear about it already, then allow me to reiterate; it's one of the most toxic and brainwashed communities you will ever come accross. This company is a psychopath when it comes to money, and the rules they have are so strict that you could even get warnings or get banned even if you don't break any rules; if you find a way to squeak the wheel and give them some harsh criticism, and keep bringing up old issues that never get addressed, you will get ♥♥♥♥ed by them. And they try to justify pretty much all of their rules behind the "but think about teh kids" argument. Bad language is strictly forbidden, but so long as you're giving them praise through it, it's totally fine. This is the game, this is where it all started. In 2001 Rockstar games released this title and made history and pretty much everyone has played this game and knows what's it about, but the question is - while being a ground breaking title more than 10 years ago, is it worth playing now and how it has aged ?
So game looks pretty good, for the time and even now-days  the graphics feels tolerable. It features day & night cycles and dynamic weather. Environment is pretty huge and worth exploring, you'll find some hidden weapons, side missions etc.
Voice acting is done pretty well, however recordings them selves are at pretty low quality, game has several radio stations with different styles of music and tracks, however I disliked pretty much every soundtrack, but maybe thats just me and for the time that music was actually pretty cool.
Story is really generic, with you leveling up and making name for yourself in underground crime scene. Game had descent number and variety of missions, starting with some more simple and ending with some quite creative goals for the time, sometimes even involving whole map. It took me about 13 hours to complete the story and do about 40-60% of side stuff.
One aspect where game have aged terribly is the game play it self. Car handling is good, but physics sometimes are just awkward and bizarre and sometimes slightest hit can make your car flip and spin like in first flat out game. Gun controls also are pretty weird, were you have to often aim at where bullets are going not where crosshair is pointed.
Missions themselves are quite challenging and more than often i found myself replaying same missions more than 3 times in row.
At the end i would recommend this game if you somehow missed this title, to see where sandbox genre has started. If you want to go and get some nostalgic feel than it's a mixed bag, with some things cool and fun to play while others just being aged and a bit frustrating.
I guess at the time game was mind blowing and had earned a lot of 10/10s, but today for me game feel's like solid 7.0.
Thanks for reading.

This game is probably my favourite space game right now.  The game includes quite a few weaponry that would make your eyes widen and includes 3 different species for you to play as.
The game's melee combat is a bit clunky and can be extremely frustrating at times, the way the melee system is this:
- Light Attack Beats Heavy Attack  (Stumbles You - If they hit you with a light attack after hiting you, you will Fall Over)
- Heavy Attack Beats Block  (Makes You Fall Over)
- Block Beats Light Attack  (Stumbles You - If they hit you with a light attack after blocking you, you will Fall Over)
The best way to do combat in Aliens vs. Predator is to always block, if you see them charging their heavy attack while you are blocking, hit them with a light attack and then again and finish them with a brutal kill or by hiting them over and over again while they're down OR if they go for a light attack, let them hit you while you block and then hit them to make them fall over and then brutal kill them or just repeatedly him them over and over again.
The game includes games modes such as Free-For-All (Everyone versus everyone), Species DeathMatch (Humans vs Predators vs Xenomorphs), Mixed Species DeathMatch (Any species on any team versus eachother) and one more (i think) but i can't remember it.
Overall the game deserves a 7/10 because the melee combat is annoying and when a predator gets his hands on a plasma cannon the xenomorphs have to either be obliterated or work together to bring him down. The humans are fine when this happens because all it takes is a human with a sniper rifle to shoot him in the head.  Also the xenomorphs wall climb can be super frustrating and disorientating when it makes you jump to the wrong wall or when your in a tight space where your xenomorph automatically goes on the walls (You can turn off auto-transition in the settings) so in my opinion this game is good but i would love to see them fix these issues or make an AVP 4 with better control for the xenomorphs.  Finally, you may not believe this but the HUMAN is actually the MOST OVERPOWERED species out of the three but feels the least coolest.  When the humans are in groups they are unstoppable, when the humans have shotguns or sniper rifles or have grenade launchers (which is a starting weapon!) they are unstoppable.  The only way to kill a human as a predator is to use stealth or long-range weapons and the only way to kill a human as a xenomorph is to catch them offguard by jumping on them from ceilings or ambush them or use flanking techniques.

HUMANS:

Gadget (You Must Pick Them Up - You Can Switch Between Them Once Picking Them Up): Plasma Cannon (High Damage Lock On Weapon that takes time to lock on and knocks enemies back - Hold The Button AND Medium Damage Freefiring weapon that doesn't lock on - Press The Button), Spear (Instant Kill Weapon), Saw Blades (Instant Kill Laser Pointing Saw Blades that follow your beam and return to you  and bounce off walls), Plasma Mines (Almost Instantly Kill when enemies step on them)

Story 10/10

Chronology of Floating Point:
- You collide into 20 walls and slow to crawl before finally making it through a bar. You are content.
- You quickly get a hang of the controls and score a few points sailing gracefully across the map. You are entertained.
- You hookshot repeatedly for many minutes and reach incredible speeds, trying to set up the perfect path, then collide with a platform by a millimeter, slow to a crawl, and sigh audibly before resigning to try all over again. You are determined.
- You finally punch the air as you watch yourself sail majestically through space, blasting through gates with incredible precision and racking up hundreds of thousands of points. You are ecstatic.
- You check the score thread and discover someone casually hit a few million in the time it took you to hit one gate, but you don't care because the gameplay is smooth as butter, the ambient sountrack is relaxing, and you can watch back your beutifully intricate, criss-crossed kaleidoscope of trails for eternity. You are addicted.

When I first saw the banners on Steam for Sleeping Dogs, I glanced over them without paying too much attention. Truth be told, movies like Hidden Moth, Crouching Panda (or whatever it's called) bore me senseless, and even as a kid, I had no interest in any marshall art stuff or hand-to-hand combat. Could a game set in Hong Kong, featuring marshall art combat hold any entertainment value for me at all?
Well, yes it could.
Sleeping Dogs is a story driven game that plays much like Grand Theft Auto, with a mission based system that reminds me more of Mafia II than the GTA series of games. In the game you play a character called Wei Shen, who is an undercover cop sent to infiltrate a dangerous gang of triads. Within the game you accept and undertake missions assigned from both the triads and the police, in an attempt to complete your assignment, maintain your cover and bring down the gang from within. In similar fashion to Mafia II and the GTA titles, missions are varied and thoroughly entertaining, with the story providing twists and turns as it unfolds.
The city looks stunning and the textures visually pleasing. Even on my dated PC, the game runs perfectly and I didn't experience any lag or bugs throughout the game. Skill leveling in Sleeping Dogs is handled by way of standing increase based on mission performance. If, for example, you kill a civilian, you'll lose some score for your police rating on that particular mission, and it'll take you longer to progress through the various police rewards.
The combat system in Sleeping Dogs reminds me, slightly, of that in the earlier Assassin's Creed games. By this I don't mean that the combat is arial, nor does it feature any form of stealth. The similarity, more specifically, is based on the mechanics that when an enemy goes to hit you, he glows red and you can then counter his move and use that momentum against him. This essentially means that with a little patience and forward planning, you can beat much bigger groups of enemies, just by waiting for them to attack, and countering their moves. As much as I detest marshall arts, this was in itself rather entertaining. In one fight, the game had me take on a group of triads, one armed with a giant meat cleaver. When he lunged at me, I broke his arm using a special move, causing him to drop the blade. I then picked it up and slaughtered him with his own cleaver, followed by everyone else in his gang.
This game only has two negative points, that I've found - and again, I'm basing these on gameplay from Mafia II and the GTA series. Firstly, it would have been nice to be able to store stolen cars in the garage. Like with the two aforementioned titles, you can steal any car on the road (excluding mission specific vehicles), but when you get back home, you can't save nor store them. If you choose that moment to save and exit game, you've lost that vehicle when you load it up again. You can, however, buy most vehicles within the game, and once bought, you can pick them up from any garage, whenever you like. This ensures that your vehicles will always be available, at any garage, but just means you need to buy that model from a dealership first. Due to the price of these cars, you'll want to buy your cars selectively.
The second negative point relates to the weapon system in the game. There are many weapons that feature within the various missions, and these are fun to play with, however once you return to your apartment and rest for the night, the weapon mysteriously vanishes. I assume this was done by design, in order to keep the focus on the marshall art element of combat. Afterall, where would the challenge be if you could simply pull out a machine gun and waste the crowd of advancing enemy gang members at the beginning of a good fight.
In closing, I'm surprised that only two of my friends already have this game. Knowing how popular the GTA series is, you'd expect this game to have greater popularity (especially considering the often reduced price in Steam Summer sales etc). If you enjoy Grand Theft Auto, Mafia II, or any of those tiresome Jackie Chan movies, you'll really enjoy Sleeping Dogs!

The best RTS you can buy at the moment and actually the one that is bringing back the genre with a logical new twist and step up.
It combines several aspects of different Strategy Subgenres, such as Build-Up Strategy (Settlers), 4X Strategy Games (CiV) or Survival Games (Banished) and mixes it with simplified mechanics of the classical RTS Genre (Warcraft or Halo Wars).
Simplified doesnt mean less complex. What makes this game great is that each single mechanic is simple by itself, but all combined form a very deep and interesting game that offers enough various ways to approach the game with new strategies and tactics.
It does have some things that are needed to fully become interesting enough, especially as a teamgame in multiplayer, which is at the moment in my eyes the weakest way to play the game, as it literally has no mechanic to interact with a teammate in a match. There is no trading with a teammate, no way to hand over resources or send units/villagers to your partner, no way to share control or anything alike that you might know from games like Age of Empires or similar.
Which is a huge mistake in my eyes.
There is a way to "trade" throug the trading post, but doing so has no impact at all and is pretty much meaningless for the other side (only for you since you get gold for doing so).
<<<<<<<Most important>>>>>>>>>>
I hope they implement a few ways to interact with teammates in a meaningful way, as it is now you just happen to play together, but you have to watch your teammate die and lose the game and you cant prevent it in any way.
If this major flaw gets solved out, this is easily the best RTS game you could get. Especially since it goes beyond simply having to attack other players, since there are peaceful ways of winning a match.

This is a truly amazing game we have here. It may be a little dated and all but there are mods for that. This game has a great introduction introducing the main character (Claude Speed) and his friend (8-Ball) who comes into the story again much later. You start doing minor jobs as a driver for a pimp/club owner. Then you do jobs for the mafia from heisting a bank truck, to delivering a corpse to cover up a murder. Again the graphics and A-I may be a little dated but the initial freedom does certainly put a smile on your face. The game has two paths you can go on: progress through the story, or just explore. To start you probably want to explore to get used to it. I'd suggest stealing a taxi and doing the taxi oddjob, which after you complete 100 fares you unlock a special taxt called the Borgnine. The police chases are endless fun as they are in any GTA game. I grew up on this game so it may warp my vision of its age a bit with nostalgia but still it is a great game. It does lack in several elements that are key in GTA games today, such as the lack of a full map and not being able to rotate the camera around your vehicle in angles that aren't 90 degrees, and the aiming is a little off but you'll get used to it. There also other versions such as the PS2 version, Xbox, and mobile Android and iOS devices (these versions do not support cheats but are easily modded). I'd heavily suggest that you play the PS2 version first to get a feel for what your getting into. The main differences between the PC and the PS2 are that PS2 has an auto targeting system and the camera isn't consistantly behind the player. See my hours? I know this game, and i know that i say it's by no reach a perfect game or a horrible one.
Congrats Chucklefish, if i could give a neutral review i would, consider this a close passmark of a release and even though this review is positive i'm still going to lay it down on you.
After spending years in early access most people assumed it would never be released and that the devs abandoned, they didn't and in fact were actively working on it throughout the time it was in early access. Their only major falter was the lack of finalized updates. I would by lying if i said i didn't at least once or twice feel angry or ripped off by Chucklefish. After all its not the money we paid, but the promises we paid for. Development is slow, very slow.
PROS:
+You will probably spend at least 100> hours exploring and getting your gameplays worth.
+Can capture any monster you find on a planet and use it as a pet (yes, its like Pokemon, but in space).
+Procedurally generated weapons, very good ones too, you will be surprised at the variety of attacks and designs.
+Building is easy, wiring is easy, painting is easy and there are hundreds upon hundreds of different blocks and decorations.
+7 Starter races that are diverse and unique.
+Modding support for this game is well maintained.
+(near) Infinite planets that never have the same two types of monster or buildings.
+Multiplayer through steam, easy to connect via the client (can be very laggy).
+Professions are chosen by the player, you can play how you want HOWEVER some professions are blatantly more fun or better than others. The Farmer will never have that awesome shotgun the explorer does or the armor the miner has.
+OST is amazing
+Active devs, who also listen a fair bit to the community. Might even find them in the Discord or IIRC.
+Customizability is insane, akin to Terraria's system (including dyes and social slots).
+Liquid and Light dynamics are "realistic"
+Supports .ABC Files (You can play actual music in game from websites such as LOTRO)
+Boss fights are unique-ish
SEMICONS: (Things that the devs are likely to fix soon, or will fix eventually, or may not be encountered by everyone)
+/- Can feel a bit solitary, especially in singleplayer
+/- Game is unoptimized and crashes on startup occasionally
+/- Mods are sometimes undetected by the game alltogether and you might have to restart multiple times to get them working
+/- Obligatory semicon about the bugs and rush to 1.0
CONS:
- AI can be pretty stupid
- The story is average, and cuts off pretty quickly with very little relevance late game.
- Some significant unbalance in both the bosses and weapons. (For their level, some are incredibly weak or easy, or very hard/OP)
- The tutorial explains gameplay fundamentals but lacks out some smaller things that people might miss
- APPLIES MAINLY TO BETA PLAYERS: If you played in beta, you will notice that a lot of content is totally gone or inconsistent, especially in tiered species weapons and the story bosses.
- Penguin crewmates are a pain in the♥♥♥♥♥br>- No ship protection in multiplayer*
- Besides farming, there is little incentive to actually build a planetary base.
- Mining can get boring quickly, especially if you are used to Terraria's systems**
- Game has a falloff point where you sit down and go "well, what next" (but that is quite some time later)
- Some mechanics seem halfbaked, where its easy to see how to improve and you are frustrated that the devs let it sit there (some bad design choices and flaws)
- Starting a new game on a server is almost impossible if the server is populated.
- Seriously, the biggest con for this game are just design flaws. Like, the hotbar for example is arguably very unintuitive and some of the aspects are left out almost completely. You will be using a feature of the game and be scratching your head "Why didn't they do ___ instead?"
- Techs are now simplified and ultimately nerfed and more boring
- Only 6 tiers? Come on, where is the 10 we had before.***
- So what are ship pets for there exactly? They do like to stand in front of my containers.
- Options screen needs a bit of a rework (if you need to explain a UI, its not a good UI)
- Wiring things in your ship can get cluttered and incredibly difficult if there are many tracks
- Matter Manipulator customization is a joke
*Any member of a party can steal or break things in your ship even still. People are divided between "simply party with people you trust" and "just give us some bloody protection options". Personally, protection options sound better because otherwise whats the point of public servers if you cant show off your ship a little bit? EDIT: After some more thought, ship protection options should just be a thing, honestly. The existence of multiplayer comes with some things you need to take for granted and one of those things are "not everyone will be a decent or honest person".
** Okay lets clear this up: Starbound is NOT a Terraria copy, YES it does have elements and inspired features that Terraria did but honestly, whats the wrong in that? Imagine how hard it would be to make a game that is nothing like any other game you've ever played. Terraria arguably perfected some aspects of the genre and there is nothing wrong with following footsteps.
*** Tiers are an iffy one, they sacrificed having 10 tiers of weapons and armor for having 6 more specialised ones; Ranged, Melee and Staffs. On top of that, where the hell are the tiered weapons for classes? They totally disappeared! In a sandbox game the idea is you have endless content and things to do - this doesn't just mean a million different blocktype, just give us some more depth and flexibility. (Should clarify, technically giving specialised class armor instead of more tiers is flexibility but it just feels cut short and i cant be the only one)
Last time i played this game on a server with friends, we didnt mine, explore, pvp, build or do quests. We all sat in a ship and played "guess the song", if that isn't simultaneously the most concerning (gameplay wise) but coolest thing then what the hell is it.
The game's development could be described as a mix of "one step forward, two steps back" and "missed opportunities" because the thing is it's easily playable but frustrating.
(removed score, decided it wasn't a good choice)
Worth the money? YES...
Runs on most computers? NO (as of right now, 1.0, which harbors some optimization problems)
Honestly i want to love Starbound i really do. To me no matter what happens now it got far enough that i enjoyed it, but was constantly disappointed in the missed opportunities

One of the most creative games I've played in recent months!

* I finished the main levels in about 45 minutes if not less, leaving only some ultra-hard levels that I gave up on almost immediately.

The truth is that I have had neither the patience nor the skill to become a decent player with other attempts at various Tower Defence games. The difficulty of the TD genre  is well known, and just like a MOBA (but in a different way of course) the learning curve is as steep as it is long.
This is the first, and perhaps most significant, success of Kingdom Rush. It eases you into the difficulty, being neither pedantic at your noobishness nor too quick to assume you've picked up the knack. This is not a polite way of saying "it's easy so I like it": I've been beaten by it on multiple times, but only because I've done something wrong or miss-timed a tower upgrade.
Its other positives are numerous and substantial. The art is blissfully cartoony and likeable whilst never being too childish or stupid. It has many references to other games and films, and although some of them are a tad clichéd, they still raise a laugh or two ("THIS IS MY BOOMSTICK!" being a tickler) But most of all, it's a joy to play. When those 3 stars pop up after a perfectly handled wave, you feel a great and long lasting sense of accomplishment. Fending off the numerous and widely varied enemies is great fun: watching hordes of Bandits and Goblins crumble in seconds to allow your towers to focus on a lumbering (and hilariously cute) Ogre really gives the player a sense of ebb and flow which continues to grow in vigorousness and length as you venture deeper into the campaign.
To summarise, Kingdom Rush is brilliant and enjoyable game. Whilst purists of the genre may argue it is a little simpler than some of its peers, I feel this is no bad thing. It pulls off a balancing act of fun and challenge that very few games even get close to mimicking.
Highly recommended to all.

TLDR "Free or Not your time is better spent on literally anything else"
Evolution RTS is a free real time strategy game based on the open source Spring engine.  The Spring engine was originally created as part of the TA Spring project which sought to bring Chris Taylor’s cult RTS “Total Annihilation” into full 3D.  Spring has since spawn a myriad of new games from TA inspired RTS games to a WWII RTS boasting multiple factions and 300 unique units.
Evolution RTS uses the Spring Lobby to setup single player and multiplayer matches. So not unlike steam games with DRM from the publisher or developer launching Evolution RTS does not start the game but actually launches the Spring Lobby which acts as a platform for playing spring engine games. During the initial Steam Release of Evolution this caused a lot of confusion since clicking “play game” didn’t actually install or even launch the game.  Obviously this♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥off a few steam users who got lost trying to navigate Spring Lobby to play the game.  It’s the same complaint that is leveled at DRM software like U-play (Spring Lobby is not DRM), it puts an unnecessary layer between the user and the game.  Certainly it doesn’t fit within the framework of the Steam platform where uses expect the game to launch from their Steam library page.
Fortunately, the developers took steps to rectify the issue by having steam load Evolution RTS and some if its popular maps in addition to the Spring Lobby. Unfortunately this still leaves users with a barrier: Spring Lobby itself. Spring Lobby isn’t terribly unintuitive and anyone with moderate computer skills should have no issues navigating it despite the fact that some UI elements are missing good tooltips. It does however move like a worm through bedrock.  It took me several minutes to setup a single player AI bot match because the interface would simply freeze each time I tried to add an AI and then again when I’d change the AI’s difficult. I honestly thought I wasn’t going to be able to pick a map, but then I typed the first few letters of the maps name and was able to select it.  The drop down menu doesn’t appear to work.
The gameplay is obviously inspired by Total Annihilation.  It uses a dual streaming resource system requiring metal and energy to construct units and buildings It deviates a bit in adding a supply system.  The game currently has a lot of the staples from the “TA Genre” including radar, land, air, and amphibious units, nukes, super units etc. but unfortunately there is only one faction to pick meaning each match feels a bit like a mirror.
Each game starts by selecting your start position.  I choose the top right corner of the map badlands because it looks like there is a lot of metal there.  I press ready and get a count down.  I start with one unit the “Overseer” which I use to construct some basic economy buildings.  The art assets, the graphics, and the animations all feel dated.  The Spring engine is no spring chicken, but there are other Spring offerings which do a far more serviceable job. Once I build my factory I get the first sign of something wrong: all my offensive units are in red like I cannot construct any of them despite having available resources.  I am unsure if this is a bug or not, but I had to restart the game 3 times before I was finally able to construct units.  In every match I played the AI parked its Overseer or commander unit in the middle of the map and never moved it when I attacked.  Fortunately it appears the AI actually knows how to build and attack.
All buildings are available for construction from the start of the game.  There doesn’t appear to be any research, upgrade, or tier system.  The constructor units don’t get an “advanced factory” to build.  Unfortunately the bad unit and building design makes this freedom pointless, I have no desire to see what units I can build.
Combat doesn’t thrill me either.  The sounds (when you can hear them over the ♥♥♥♥♥♥ dubstep soundtrack) are pretty generic, the units explode leaving no wreckage. Units don’t seem to have much in the way of hit points meaning your army won’t last very long before exploding.  .  I tried building defensive towers but found them destroyed quickly by even light scout units.  It’s obvious the game lacks any semblance of balance.  At this point in my play through I couldn’t handle another minute of the soundtrack which felt completely out of place in an RTS game, but right at home in a 12 year olds Call of Duty video.  When I saw that the options menu was devoid of any content and I couldn’t shut off the direct feed to some wannabe-skrillex’s soundcloud page.  I had to stop.
Do not play this game. Amateur doesn’t even describe it, early access doesn’t describe, it isn’t worth the 5 – 10 minutes it takes to set it up.  Free or not pass on this one.  If you’re feeling nostalgic about Chris Taylor RTS games there are plenty of better Spring offerings, TA on GOG, and an active community around SupCom FA called FA Forever. If you’re looking for fresh RTS blood move along, you won’t find that here either.  To anyone who says why are you knocking a free game?  Well because the developers are offering it to people as a way to spend their free time.  This is a commodity as much as money is.  Trust me on this one
Your free time is better spent elsewhere.

In Sleeping Dogs youm play as a character called Wei Shen in Hong Kong and you return from America. You will soon be part of gangs and the Police after you. Some people say that they cant run it well but because I have AMD and the game runs best on AMD cards I dont have a problem.
+ The voice acting in Sleeping Dogs is amazing since they have some famous people voice acting which seems flawless. There is no bad points on the voice acting in the game. Everyone sounds diffrent which works well thoughtout the game.

- The cars are really hard to drive in since they turn so much. You turn left for more than one second and your car will fly into the building and is horrible since it sould have been so much better. There is no sensitivity option from what I know.
Overall I think Sleeping Dogs is a great and unique game with lots to do and lots of things to see. I sure do hope that they wil make a Sleeping Dogs 2 since it really deserves it! I am going to rate Sleepung Dogs 9 out of 10, at great game and lots to do. I would recommend this game to anyone who can run it.

Welp, the game has declared itself released now; so I suppose its as good a time as any to review it.
I've been with this little project since its conception; and I have to say, I'm pretty disappointed. Don't get me wrong, it is most certianly a good investment for 15 dollars; and I have no doubt in my mind that plenty of people will get plenty of enjoyment out of it. Heck, I got a pretty decent amount of fun from it too. Why am I disappointed then? I mean, I certianly got my moneys worth right? Well, I am disappointed becuase this isn't the game I backed.
Originally: Ore and metal were procedurally generated, not just positions but the actual properties of the resources, every planet was to have a variety of unique ores to discover, no two sets alike.
Now: There's a set tiering system similar to terraria.
Originally: Your crew was supposed to be an invalueble asset to your space travel; you would have an engineering, science, and military portion. Your engineers would assemble things like drop ships, mechs, guns. Your Scientists would research the stuff you brought back from different worlds.
Now: Build a house, place a colony deed, and do some quests; now you can report an NPC that might give you a passive buff on your ship or act as a companion on quests.
Originally: Space ship upgrades were modular and had variety; you could also build space stations and other interesting structures.
Now: Upgrades are linear, you go from one to the other with no interesting changes added besides more space to your ship.
Originally: Every race had a unique back story that described why exactly it was you were in your destroyed space ship above an underexplored planet. Whether it was a search for the meaning of life; or an attempt at a rebellion against oppression; this games plots were supposed to be branching and interesting.
Now: Everyones the member of some group called the "Protectorate" which is your super basic group of do-gooders that just want to make the universe a better place. Also there's a giant tenticle monster. Neat.
There's probably a bunch of stuff I'm forgetting; the point here is, this game is a very different beast than the one I backed way back in the day. I guess that's just the gamble you take when you back a game early on.
All that being said though; its a fun enough experience with friends that should offer you a neat space sandbox exploration game. With mods who knows? Maybe someone can deliver what the devs promised.

Kingdom Rush is a very enjoyable tower defense game. It has a very nice look and feel. The difficulty seems somewhat imbalanced. I had no problems to finish some levels on hard, while some levels were very difficult even on easy. The first half of the game was more fun, there was a lot of progress and new things. The second half had some interesting new enemies, but there was no more development in towers or heroes, which is a pity.
The fact that you can't place your towers anywhere, just on designated spots, changes the tower defense concept quite a bit. Some people might like it, some might not. Kingdom Rush also usually gives you quite low amount of money, so you have to carefully plan what you build and where. Instead of just playing spontaneously as in other TD games, this makes this particular game also close to a strategy/puzzle game. If you don't plan carefully the tower layout from the very early beginning, nothing will help you.

I played the first half of the game before going to bed one night.
I didn't know what to expect, and I was pleasantly surprised.
The game perfectly captures what it's like to be a small shapeshifting triangle drifting between abstract planes to 140 beats per minute of ambient techno music. It was a mesmerizing experience.
The puzzles are simple but clever. Parts of it are very challenging, but well-placed checkpoints keep you grooving to the beat even when you make a mistake (except in the "hardcore" second half of the game). However mind-bending and challenging the puzzles got, the overall feel of the game was very therapeutic and flowy.
The screenshots don't look like they make any sense - even to me, but they all make sense at the time. You have to play it to understand.
The game ended when I was ready for it to end, but it is a short game, and part of me wishes there was more. My hopes were raised when I discovered the hardcore levels, but after a few attempts, my frustration got the better of me.
I didn't try it, but I recommend trying the game after getting high first.

Bastion is a brilliant little game with an amazing plot and engrossing narrative. You'll be engaged each step of the way.
Where Bastion really shines is in the balance of the gameplay elements itself. The developer has kept the RPG customization options to an appropriate limit for a game of this size. While some games delve very deep into inventories, skill trees, and talents (appropriately), Bastion keeps it pretty simple. The player is left with a smaller set of choices to make and instead is able to focus on what playstyle is better suited to the encounter and ultimately, what they enjoy the most.
For the price it's currently going for there is absolutely no reason that you shouldn't snag up Bastion when you get a chance. You won't regret it!

I only completed the three 'normal' levels.., but I can safely say that this game is worth 5$ whether you beat the bonus levels or not, hands down. It's short and sweet for someone who's familiar with rhythm, and an enticing challenge for those who aren't. I fall into the latter group. I've never been musically inclined myself, but the concept is spectacular and beautifully executed. The background is comprised of sound bars that aren't just for show; they really do reflect the behavior of the music, which is an integral part of the game.
The main objective as a platformer is to retrieve orbs that, for solidarity, I'll call beat orbs. These orbs can be deposited in various parts of the map in subwoofer-esque circles in the floor to add a new beat to the music and influence the behavior of the map. Indeed, there are far too few visual ques(The fact that it's minimalistic is just a bonus) for you to be able to succeed without training your ears to the music. Every little action produces a sound just like in real life, and bringing yourself in tune with these intermingling sounds and focusing on individual sounds are the key to success. I won't say similar things haven't been done before (See:
), but never have they been done quite like this.
Normally I'm very critical of anything with less than three dimensions, call it a character flaw if you must... but this game does something that simply can't be done in 3d and for that I applaud this game.
I also recorded my experiences with the game if you'd like to see what you're getting for your money.

This is simply one of the best implimentations of the tower defense genre.  With the appealing art style, stiff challenge, variety of enemy units, polished and deep tower mechanics, and wide variety of hero units, this game is a standout among an otherwise tired genre.

Maddeningly bad route finding (the game was made in 2012!?), which leads to the need for micromanaging all (land) units which frequently get stuck or pile up into a 3- or 4-vehicle traffic jam. Therefore your supporting vehicles are not available for assistance when you really need them. It also happens that they are out of ammo because they have been firing away at untargetable units (so much for defensive stance), which can be embarrassing when you are in a tight corner. Sometimes units simply won't carry out orders (and no, their program was not suspended). In short: the AI is simply BAD.
Ridiculously small action radius of vehicles (some 5 km on a full tank?), while it's unclear how this makes the game more interesting.
Moreover, the 1st person game play (when on foot) is rather bland.

In simple terms, if you have played supreme commander and liked it, you will absolutely like this as well.
However, if you did not enjoy playing supreme commander or despise micromanagement RTS games, this isn't for you.
For those who are interested, some free tips upon joining the game...
First, what you are downloading from steam is just a server platform. Not the game itself.
Secondly, once you join a server room (in the multiplayer tab, duh!), you are automatically allocated as a spectator. You will not be allowed to pick a team and play until you have downloaded the game contents and its map for the particular match (all of which will be done for you automatically so do not worry, just wait a bit once you've joined).
Thirdly, after you have completed the download process, join a team or create a team.
Lastly, click start and enjoy. It will play the same way as supreme commander so it will come to you naturally. Only difference is that the buildings and units names are different.
My final advice for newcomers - Join as a spectator and take a look at how others play. You have free movement as a spectator.

140 is a platformer. While this seems like a fairly simplistic asessment of the game, it is nonetheless the most apt description of it, as 140 is also a fairly simple game. what makes it stand apart from others is perhaps the fact that visually, it is quite strike, with bold colours changing constantly, and nary more that a square or circle in terms of geometry. The visuals aren't lazy though, with fluid animations and some obvious effort in creating a unique style. Perhaps a major draw is the relationship with the music, with many of the platforming segments relying on rhythm to complete, and some of the background visual elements being connected to the music that is playing. There are also boss levels which change the gameplay completely, one being a pseudo shoot em up, another being a boss fight which uses rhythm and posistion.
140 is, for the most part, a fairly decent game. Whether or not it's woth getting for it's price point (currently at $5.00), thats another matter entirely. If you get it as part of a bigger bundle, or if you can get it for < $2, you'll have some fun with it, but otherwise, it's too short and too limited in scope to actually be worth $5.00.

This is the first Mortal Kombat game I have played so far and it won't be the last I'm sure.
It's a really enjoyable fighting game that offers a lot of complexity but is not to difficult to understand.
It provides you with more moves per character and some preset combos unlike street fighter for example which I am having a hard time getting into. It seems to be a bit more forgiving for beginners but does reward skillful play just the same.
Having played quite a couple of fighting games this seems like a nice middle ground for me between the hardcore streetfighter and tekken for example that makes stuff like long combos via juggling not all to difficult.
The game does offer a lot of kontent (see what I did there?) with a challenging but very enjoyable story mode that blends the fights and what happens between them into one thing without having to go through any loading times whatsoever and countless challenge mode levels.
The roster is quite big and every character does have a good set of unique moves, which are really fun to combine in the tag team mode which lets other characters assist sort of like marvel vs capcom/tekken tag.
The only downside is that like some others may have reported the netcode isnt very good. There was a very noticeable lag when playing with some of my friends that made it very hard to execute some moves or react in time.
If you happen to looking for a really good fighting game, veteran or new to the genre alike and don't mind keeping it to the various single player modes until (if its even happening) the multiplayer gets a little more love then I do recommend this without regrets.

Not too sure what to write here so heres a recipe for Pancakes instead
Ingredients:
1 1/2 cups all-purpose flour
3 tablespoons sugar
1 tablespoon baking powder
1/4 teaspoon salt
1/8 teaspoon freshly ground nutmeg
2 large eggs, at room temperature
1 1/4 cups milk, at room temperature
1/2 teaspoon pure vanilla extract
3 tablespoons unsalted butter, plus more as needed
Now to make it
1. In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, sugar, baking powder, salt, and nutmeg.
2. In another bowl, beat the eggs and then whisk in the milk and vanilla.
3. Melt the butter in a large cast iron skillet or griddle over medium heat.
4. Whisk the butter into the milk mixture. Add the wet ingredients to the flour mixture, and whisk until a thick batter is just formed
5. Keeping the skillet at medium heat, ladle about 1/4 cup of the batter onto the skillet, to make a pancake. Make 1 or 2 more pancakes, taking care to keep them evenly spaced apart. Cook, until bubbles break the surface of the pancakes, and the undersides are golden brown, about 2 minutes. Flip with a spatula and cook about 1 minute more on the second side. Serve immediately or transfer to a platter and cover loosely with foil to keep warm. Repeat with the remaining batter, adding more butter to the skillet as needed.
6. Procedure for adding fruit to pancakes: Once the bubbles break the surface of the pancakes, scatter the surface with sliced or diced fruit, or chocolate chips, nuts, etc. Flip with a spatula and cook for 1 minute more, being careful not to burn toppings.

McPixel is an over-the-top silly point-n-click (PnC) episodic adventure game.  You have a few seconds in each episode to figure out what to do with a bomb.  First you have to find it, then you have to figure out what to do with it.  You are typically only allowed to make only one or two decisions, and see how your decision plays out.  Losing is not only part of the game, but is sometimes rewarded.  In each scenario, you want to fulfill each possibility each one has to offer to get a 100% rating.  As long as you don't repeat an action already taken, you can unlock bonus stages.  The game is simply a fun romp through twisted and bizarre worlds, with surprises around every corner.  As a bonus, you can even create your own scenarios, and download user and developer made scenarios as well.  All DLC is free, so replay value is high.  Give it a shot.

This is the game that started it all - the craze of third person, open world sandbox games. GTA III has a immersive story that you follow, and along the way, wreak havok on Liberty City to your heart's content. With a varied range of weapons and vehicles, achieve your goals in any way you feel like it, or just explore what Liberty City has to offer. Time has not been so kind to the graphics of GTA III, and animations are a bit wonky and broken, but that doesn't detract from the fun that will be had during the whole game. On top of all this as well the game features fleshed out characters and stories than few games had achieved at the time, and a very memorable soundtrack.
Replayability, unfortunately, is one of GTA III's shortcomings as there's not much to engage in after the main story has been passed, save for rather bland side missions, and blowing up Liberty City for the 100th time, there's not much after to look forward to. 8.6/10

I like the concept of this; I'm a huge fan of games that are heavily tied into the audio. The objective is to gather multi-colored orbs and bring them to these half-circle zones nearby. Each orb adds more complexity to both the soundtrack and the level, and opens up more of it. While the controls are pretty simple, some of the platforming does require perfect timing. Platforms move and/or disappear in time with the music, which actually helps, because it allows you to work out the timing required.
At least in the first three worlds, there's no penalty for death. You simply start back at the last checkpoint. I'm not sure if that continues on. It can be kind of frustrating, since some of the timing does need to be precise, and the boss fights can take a few run throughs to work out the pattern.
I enjoy the music, which is pretty beat-heavy electronica. I do think this is one of those games that would not be kind to anyone with any sort of photosensitivity; the visuals aren't quite neon, but they do tend to change and flash with regularity.

You may be too impatient to get this game working. As a fan of Orcs must Die, which was a game of similar gameplay, i ♥♥♥♥ing love this game.
Join Skye, Sweet, SiMo and Haigen, as well as TSYGAN if you bought the DLC, as they defend the cores from a horde of dangerous alien creatures called Lumes. There's more to it, because this game actually has a plot. It's pretty good, i'd say. A bit basic, but good.
The gameplay is fantastic. You build towers, and then you defend the core from the Lumes. But wait. The towers aren't doing all the work, YOU are helping out as well, you lazy twit. You get a good amount of weaponry to shoot the aliens with, and a variety of perks to bolster you and your defenses, and they vary from quite basic guns, to some pretty strange guns. And if you suck at aiming, don't worry. There are a few perks and guns that help counter that. You do have to do SOME aiming, ESPECIALLY in the last level of the first DLC.
The scenery is goddamn gorgeous, and they didn't even put borders around the arena, so you are free to explore the area. Do watch your step, even more so when you are playing Sweet, because there are some bottomless pits. And blasting yourself in the wrong direction can very quickly end in some fund losses in hospital bills. Well, not really, you get to keep the money. You will just have some SEVERE pain in your legs for a while. You can walk it off.
If you are looking for more, there is a whole DLC campaign that continues where the base game leaves off. The quality varies quite a bit in terms of maps and towers, but all of them are pretty good. A gripe i have is that the AA tower, which you will NEED early on in the DLC, is locked behind rank 32. So you'll have to defend a bit untill then.
So yeah, Sanctum 2 is a pretty good game. Even more so if you play Co-oP. So, if you dig a strangely holy concoction
of TD and FPS, i'd highly suggest you pick this one up.

UPDATE 4/20/14
In light of the recent update, it's necessary I update my review with it, to maintain accuracy. The original contents are below.
The layout of the game lobby has improved dramatically. I was actually able to start a game through Single Player mode, fairly independent of the multiplayer lobby. That doesn't mean I actually had any idea how to play the game at that point, but it was a start.
I received comments that the issues in my previous review were resolved; they weren't. Not the main ones. I need to say, the lobby still doesn't seem user-friendly enough for newbies to join right in. The major unaddressed problem was the absence of documentation or instructions for the lobby, and now that I can start a game, a lack of game rules or a tutorial came into play too. If there are rules available somewhere, they aren't visible enough for me to find them. (If there are instructions on the Spring site, link 'em to me please.)
With the new update, the game has really upped its... game (snort). It’s much improved, but only relative to its ease to start with. There are legit unresolved problems that even the new update didn’t address, and are probably keeping the more inexperienced off of their doorstep. It's difficult because I really want to give this game a shot- but I've spent over two hours messing around with the game and lobby settings, and haven't even been able to blow anything up. I really need some direction for me to recommend this game, but for now it's too undeveloped for me to stick a “yes” on it.
UPDATE 5/4/14
I'm holding true to my promise that I would update this further.

To start, the first thing even close to help I received was the developer finding my review and labeling me as “not using my noggin” when dealing with in-game commands. I'm not holding grudges, our issues are resolved. The lobby is scary, in-game less so, and it's all expected to be figured out by the player, as made evident by the developer. Apparently it was not just me who wasn't able to build something so simple as generators, which was seen as obvious and common sense during development and doesn't require explanation (however, the developer did design a very helpful piece of video tutorial, just for me, that can be found in the comments or here:

The download for the game is simply a download for a game lobby.
OH GOD WHY.
I hung around for around 25 minutes trying to figure out how to just start a game. The Terms of Service for the Spring Engine lobby were easy to read, props for that. After spending years in early access most people assumed it would never be released and that the devs abandoned, they didn't and in fact were actively working on it throughout the time it was in early access. Their only major falter was the lack of finalized updates. I would by lying if i said i didn't at least once or twice feel angry or ripped off by Chucklefish. After all its not the money we paid, but the promises we paid for. Development is slow, very slow.
PROS:
+You will probably spend at least 100> hours exploring and getting your gameplays worth.
+Can capture any monster you find on a planet and use it as a pet (yes, its like Pokemon, but in space).
+Procedurally generated weapons, very good ones too, you will be surprised at the variety of attacks and designs.
+Building is easy, wiring is easy, painting is easy and there are hundreds upon hundreds of different blocks and decorations.
+7 Starter races that are diverse and unique.
+Modding support for this game is well maintained.
+(near) Infinite planets that never have the same two types of monster or buildings.
+Multiplayer through steam, easy to connect via the client (can be very laggy).
+Professions are chosen by the player, you can play how you want HOWEVER some professions are blatantly more fun or better than others. The Farmer will never have that awesome shotgun the explorer does or the armor the miner has.
+OST is amazing
+Active devs, who also listen a fair bit to the community. Might even find them in the Discord or IIRC.
+Customizability is insane, akin to Terraria's system (including dyes and social slots).
+Liquid and Light dynamics are "realistic"
+Supports .ABC Files (You can play actual music in game from websites such as LOTRO)
+Boss fights are unique-ish
SEMICONS: (Things that the devs are likely to fix soon, or will fix eventually, or may not be encountered by everyone)
+/- Can feel a bit solitary, especially in singleplayer
+/- Game is unoptimized and crashes on startup occasionally
+/- Mods are sometimes undetected by the game alltogether and you might have to restart multiple times to get them working
+/- Obligatory semicon about the bugs and rush to 1.0
CONS:
- AI can be pretty stupid
- The story is average, and cuts off pretty quickly with very little relevance late game.
- Some significant unbalance in both the bosses and weapons. (For their level, some are incredibly weak or easy, or very hard/OP)
- The tutorial explains gameplay fundamentals but lacks out some smaller things that people might miss
- APPLIES MAINLY TO BETA PLAYERS: If you played in beta, you will notice that a lot of content is totally gone or inconsistent, especially in tiered species weapons and the story bosses.
- Penguin crewmates are a pain in the♥♥♥♥♥br>- No ship protection in multiplayer*
- Besides farming, there is little incentive to actually build a planetary base.
- Mining can get boring quickly, especially if you are used to Terraria's systems**
- Game has a falloff point where you sit down and go "well, what next" (but that is quite some time later)
- Some mechanics seem halfbaked, where its easy to see how to improve and you are frustrated that the devs let it sit there (some bad design choices and flaws)
- Starting a new game on a server is almost impossible if the server is populated.
- Seriously, the biggest con for this game are just design flaws. Like, the hotbar for example is arguably very unintuitive and some of the aspects are left out almost completely. You will be using a feature of the game and be scratching your head "Why didn't they do ___ instead?"
- Techs are now simplified and ultimately nerfed and more boring
- Only 6 tiers? Come on, where is the 10 we had before.***
- So what are ship pets for there exactly? They do like to stand in front of my containers.
- Options screen needs a bit of a rework (if you need to explain a UI, its not a good UI)
- Wiring things in your ship can get cluttered and incredibly difficult if there are many tracks
- Matter Manipulator customization is a joke
*Any member of a party can steal or break things in your ship even still. People are divided between "simply party with people you trust" and "just give us some bloody protection options". Personally, protection options sound better because otherwise whats the point of public servers if you cant show off your ship a little bit? EDIT: After some more thought, ship protection options should just be a thing, honestly. The existence of multiplayer comes with some things you need to take for granted and one of those things are "not everyone will be a decent or honest person".
** Okay lets clear this up: Starbound is NOT a Terraria copy, YES it does have elements and inspired features that Terraria did but honestly, whats the wrong in that? Imagine how hard it would be to make a game that is nothing like any other game you've ever played. Terraria arguably perfected some aspects of the genre and there is nothing wrong with following footsteps.
*** Tiers are an iffy one, they sacrificed having 10 tiers of weapons and armor for having 6 more specialised ones; Ranged, Melee and Staffs. On top of that, where the hell are the tiered weapons for classes? They totally disappeared! In a sandbox game the idea is you have endless content and things to do - this doesn't just mean a million different blocktype, just give us some more depth and flexibility. (Should clarify, technically giving specialised class armor instead of more tiers is flexibility but it just feels cut short and i cant be the only one)
Last time i played this game on a server with friends, we didnt mine, explore, pvp, build or do quests. We all sat in a ship and played "guess the song", if that isn't simultaneously the most concerning (gameplay wise) but coolest thing then what the hell is it.
The game's development could be described as a mix of "one step forward, two steps back" and "missed opportunities" because the thing is it's easily playable but frustrating.
(removed score, decided it wasn't a good choice)
Worth the money? YES...
Runs on most computers? NO (as of right now, 1.0, which harbors some optimization problems)
Honestly i want to love Starbound i really do. To me no matter what happens now it got far enough that i enjoyed it, but was constantly disappointed in the missed opportunities

Welp, the game has declared itself released now; so I suppose its as good a time as any to review it.
I've been with this little project since its conception; and I have to say, I'm pretty disappointed. Don't get me wrong, it is most certianly a good investment for 15 dollars; and I have no doubt in my mind that plenty of people will get plenty of enjoyment out of it. Heck, I got a pretty decent amount of fun from it too. Why am I disappointed then? I mean, I certianly got my moneys worth right? Well, I am disappointed becuase this isn't the game I backed.
Originally: Ore and metal were procedurally generated, not just positions but the actual properties of the resources, every planet was to have a variety of unique ores to discover, no two sets alike.
Now: There's a set tiering system similar to terraria.
Originally: Your crew was supposed to be an invalueble asset to your space travel; you would have an engineering, science, and military portion. Your engineers would assemble things like drop ships, mechs, guns. Your Scientists would research the stuff you brought back from different worlds.
Now: Build a house, place a colony deed, and do some quests; now you can report an NPC that might give you a passive buff on your ship or act as a companion on quests.
Originally: Space ship upgrades were modular and had variety; you could also build space stations and other interesting structures.
Now: Upgrades are linear, you go from one to the other with no interesting changes added besides more space to your ship.
Originally: Every race had a unique back story that described why exactly it was you were in your destroyed space ship above an underexplored planet. Whether it was a search for the meaning of life; or an attempt at a rebellion against oppression; this games plots were supposed to be branching and interesting.
Now: Everyones the member of some group called the "Protectorate" which is your super basic group of do-gooders that just want to make the universe a better place. Also there's a giant tenticle monster. Neat.
There's probably a bunch of stuff I'm forgetting; the point here is, this game is a very different beast than the one I backed way back in the day. I guess that's just the gamble you take when you back a game early on.
All that being said though; its a fun enough experience with friends that should offer you a neat space sandbox exploration game. With mods who knows? Maybe someone can deliver what the devs promised.

Town of Salem started off as a flash game to play online on your web browser and is now about £4 on the steam store for you to play! I'd personally buy it on sale when it is 50% off.
Town of Salem is a game about lies, deception, wit, courage, luck and skill to work your way through in getting rid of anyone opposing you whether you are a Mafia member or Jester. For anyone that has played the card game Werewolf or Mafia, Town of Salem is extremely similar to it, adding in new and fun roles for you to try out ranging from a Retributionist to a damn Vampire Hunter, like, how cool is that?!
There are some problems and it can't be a game without it: gamethrowers are a big problem, ruining the fun for everyone (Mostly Mafia members if a Mafia member was killed, revealing other people when he/she dies); from what I hear, the staff aren't exactly helping with these issues either.
It is hilariously fun to play with your friends especially at 2AM where you just have no clue what you are doing anymore, or being a Vigilante and shooting every single Mafia member consecutively every night, damn that is satisfying.
Want to be a specific role? Just buy a scroll. They give you times 10 odds of becoming that role, not exactly guaranteed but still a bigger chance than normal!
I would definitely reccomended this game to anyone who loves to think logically and enjoys a challenge!

Disclaimer: I received a key for this from a third-party administered giveaway. This was not in exchange for any consideration such as a positive review. Which is good, since I would have trashed it anyway had it deserved it. ;)
Anyway, now with that out of the way, this is a top-down wave survival shooter. Bunches of enemies spawn in, you shoot or blow them up, more spawn in until you die or survive all the waves. In this case the enemies are pink aliens that want to eat your brain. No deceptive game title here. You get a flashlight and a selection of 6 weapons you'll get and upgrade by making kills. Fairly standard shooter fare, but well done. You can play solo or in coop with up to 4 players. Again the gameplay is nothing that hasn't been done at some point or another elsewhere, but this is solidly executed and the fun factor is there.
The visuals are in a blocky retroish 3D style, with a nice color contrast between the pink aliens and the environments. I like the look myself. The sound is solid but unremarkable. There are cards, achievements, and leaderboards. The achievements will require skill to 100% without being ridiculous, so those are a plus.
In summary, this treads absolutely no new ground, but it does what it does well. If you like top down survive the waves shooters you should like this one. Recommended, at a price point to be determined by the reader.

So freaking good. Almost five years later, it's a timeless masterpiece that you just want to keep playing more and more.
At its core, it's a pretty simple story but it manages to charm and captivate like no other. The voiceover narration embedded into the gameplay is so expertly done. The soundtrack is easily one of the best ever in any form of entertainment, creating a new genre by itself.
Combat it very satisfying and the game encourages you to try out different weapon combos and experiment with upgrades. There's plenty of totally optional "proving grounds" where, even if you fail the challenge, you learn something about how to best use a certain weapon. It's really well designed.
The the upgrading and weapons system is quite in-depth for a game that looks so deceptively simple and playful from its tone. Passive bonuses from potions are great. There's a dynamic difficulty system where the player intentionally makes the game harder for themselves in exchange for more EXP, which is genius.
All the areas are diverse and different enough so that you don't ever feel like you're doing the same thing twice. The handpainted environments are drop-dead gorgeous, only enhanced by the amazing soundtrack.
I could go on for hours, but just buy the game. It's that good.

2 hours of exhilarating and pulsating fun. Play through several screens of colorful geometrical figures that move and dance in rhythm with the background music. You might even wanna snap a couple of these screens and use them as wallpapers on your HD monitors. Background music does not just direct the movements of puzzle pieces, but also is the means to unlock the path ahead since you will need to time your moves according to the beats. Puzzles are intelligent and will amaze you when you've figured out their solutions. There are, in total, three levels, and at the end of each level, you are challenged with a boss screen. The third level, however, has two boss screens, the last one of which is a disappointment since it is solvable with a fixed sequence of key presses ONLY however many times you play it. I like this game in particular above many other puzzlers as it doesn't test you on how good you are at your keyboard, but instead your patience and alertness by offering you unlimited time for each puzzle piece.
A solid 9/10.

God damn this TD completely blew my mind, I bought it as I saw it featured on a humble sale and I thought "Hey, I haven't played TD in ages, this one looks fun.". Turns out I haven't played such luxurious one since Gem TD as well. Art is cartoony and very cute. Also, unexpectedly rich for an indie game. Large amount of monsters, locations, heroes, towers, tower upgrades. You always have something new to notice and look at. From the big picture view, design is standard with expected TD patters, nothing new. However, developers gave huge focus to design details that make you fall in love with the game. You will start to notice them right away and uncover much more through the campaign. This is what makes the game so amazing. Funny voice responses of heroes full of various references to games, movies, etc. Map easter eggs to discover and interact with (sheeps, windmills, ...). Gameplay is very smooth and well designed. You can play it casually, enjoying your time, or like a pro, thinking of crisp timings and deep strategies. Simply put, playing this game will give you a great satisfaction from many different views whoever you are. I just can't recommend this gem from Ironhide Game Studio enough.
About drawbacks, there are few I would like to mention: First, the waypoints and reactions of melee tower soldiers... I am quite experienced in Blizzard strategy games and these melee units are completely unituitive for someone like me. At the same time I believe they made it intentionally this awkward to keep balance and give space to more try-hard players. Second, I feel like every level requires a certain strategy which you have to uncover and successfully use, experimenting different builds usually ends up in a failure. Last, there is no level editor. I understand this game came from its web/mobile predecessor, but giving space to talented and passionate players might yield so many interesting levels and patterns I would love to see and understand.

140 is a great minimalist, hardcore platforming game with a unique twist: the level changes to the beat of the music. Platforms will appear, grow, shrink, move, blink out of existence, or become deadly to touch at the beat. Walls and hazards will rhythmically turn on and off. It's really very cool. You are an entrepid little monochromatic shape braving the dangers of the three levels and overcoming the bosses at the end of each. If you manage to beat them all, you will be granted an even more challenging adventure (and seriously, the last boss is a huge jerk. Like, really really mean.) I just beat the entire game (and unlocked all achievements, which was nice), and it took me about 6 hours, which is impressive considering if done perfectly, you could probably do the whole game in less than 15 minutes. I think it was worth the money spent.
I love the simplicity of the game's graphics, controls, and objectives, I love the precision and timing involved, and I love the music for this game! The only thing I can think of that I don't like about this game is what happens when you die... I die a lot, and every time it happens I jump out of my chair... If you like heart attacks, seriously pick up this game.
As a final note, this game is on sale ALL THE TIME. you can either wait and grab it for $1-$3, or support the dev and maybe help them get more games out by paying full price, which I recommend.

So, what is 140? It is a minimal, abstract platform game. Aside from that, it is a really cool platform rhythm game. The levels start out "simple" the music isn't too complicated. As you get to checkpoints, more complex rhythms are put into the soundtrack and these make other things happen: blocks appear and disappear, shapes grow and shrink, static fields jump, bouncy floors activate, gravity shifts. Paying attention to the music and how it affects the level is crucial to finishing. At the end of each level there is a boss fight. Each level the boss fights get more complex.
Once you have finished the game three mirror levels open up. One wrong move and you fail - you must complete the entire level without dying. And all the patterns are backwards. Yeah right.
Funny but short platform game.

While certainly enjoyable and creative ,much of the challenge of the game is the requirement for "perfect" play. It is certainly a pleasure for a game to reveal its internal rules during play and  it can especially tricky to facilitate communicating these mechanics to the player without the (sadly common) excessive use of text or game-immersion-breaking tutorials. The use of audio to communicate game mechanics is not a unique idea but it is certainly novel and implemented in a very stylisticly unique way here.  A distinctive aesthetic, with a colour palette that either harks back to the Commodore 64 Era or is instead very modern (all that is old is new again)
Very pleasant to listen to and look at and handles very well.
However: 140 is not without criticism. The paradigm of 'either Perfection or Failure' is (to me) a very old fashioned design choice and not one that is particularly endearing as repeating some sections can quickly become tedious.
The "bosses" are a particular nuisance and rapidly became annoyances to be overcome, 'gates' of memorization and tedium to pass through to get to the next level.
On the checkpointing system, it may actually be this that lets the game down.
Despite VVVVVV being, as a friend put it “Ba***rd hard”, the use of checkpoints allowed the less dexterous of us to muddle through without losing our minds in frustration. The delay in getting back to the action when hitting static also seems just a little too long, which detracts from the experience slightly.
A gamepad is recommended.
Overall quite good, would not recommend to those without good rhythm or spatial reasoning.
