Retro game crunch is a collection of games that resemble NES games of old. This has many
genres leading to quite a bit of variation. The music Also has A lot of effort put into it, as none of these games have a bad soundtrack. Each game does vary in quality in other regards so I will try and break it down.
Super chew land- Reminds me a lot of E.V.O. The search for eden on the SNES but focused more on exploring. You eat to evolve and as you evolve you can explore the area more. And also unlike E.V.O. You can't choose how to evolve, but it makes up for it with exploration and some puzzle solving. I should mention the boss is really well designed and fun. One of the better games on the pack.
End of line-this is more on the puzzle side of the collection. It's really good as it does a fine job at scaling the difficulty and teaching new mechanics quickly. You are trying to destroy repair bots so you can destroy yourself(the repair bots heal you when you die) and it can get complicated with different forms and traps. I should also mention this has my favorite soundtracks in the collection. The downside is later in the game it can have a bit too much trial and error and can get frustrating. Still one of the better games on here.
Gaia attack-A beat-em up/platformer that's pretty fun. It feels satisfying to hit enemies and does a great job in feeling retro, more so than the other games. The down side is that it's rather short. Only four stages(there is a scoring and leader board for replays though). And like many brawlers it does get repetitive(so maybe it being short isn't that bad). One of the better games in this collection
Wub Wub Wescue-A game in the same vain as the classic arcade game donkey kong. It has
interesting ideas involving record's giving you power over enemies and slowing down time. The design of the dog is also really cute. The music does a good job at giving a very big jungle vibe considering it's 8-bit. I do feel the first two acts start off slow. Around act three though it starts picking up. Also some of the puzzles are a bit annoying.I should say kind of in between as far as my favorites here, but I can see others getting more out of it.
Paradox Lost-A very metroid style game that has it's ups and downs. You travel through time and explore, finding captives and power ups. Though it's most interesting feature leads to it's biggest issues. The level design can be really confusing since you have three eras to navigate and the eras all overlap. This can also make backtracking a pain since it's easy to go the wrong way. This might be just me but, I also had some bad glitches when I moved through time. Sometimes I wouldn't go through to a different era only to go through the second time (in the same spot) and that might be due to enemies but it did make me get lost a few times. At one point I passed through time and glitched into a wall and warped to the other side of the map. These issues are disappointing as this had the most potential in the collection. As it stands it's the most frustrating to play.
Brains and hearts-A card game in the vain of...well anything you'd do with a deck of cards, and hard for me to review as I'm not a card player. The rules aren't complicated and the rules are set up so you can always do something every turn. I don't find anything wrong with it really, as far as card games go. But I can't dive into it like the others so I have to stay neutral on this one, but if you like card games I don't see why this would let you down.
Shuten- A shoot'em up that feels the most complete to me and is my favorite in this collection.Fast  paced and lot's of upgrades and weapons. You can take weapons from enemies in the middle of game play, leading to lot's of variation. The enemies all have different but predictable patterns but it throws a lot at once. So you can mess up quick, but you can deflect shot's back at enemies with your sword(separate from your weapon) making the game have tense moments. It's not perfect though, while the bosses are good, I don't like the recycled ones very much, as it feels a bit repetitive after multiple times. And maybe it's just me but the last level has a massive difficulty spike. It has a ton of enemies everywhere and the last boss is multi-formed with the most difficult patterns in the game. Replay levels and upgrade a lot is all I have to say.
Overall while I like some of these more than others, it's worth a look. I'm not sure if it's
worth full price but I do recommend it.

You are nameless commando guy, your goal: destroy a sea of droids and reach the exit elevator. Where this game really shines is it's customization and music. You collect money and chips which you use to buy and upgrade weapons, armour and accessories. There is a good of each and they really allow for a lot of different playstyles. The music is perfect and keeps you pumped. The gameplay is repetitive but really fun and addicting. Enemies are challenging and can kill you quick if your not prepared so killing them stays satisfying, even when your grinding for that next item. The level design keeps things fresh by featuring wave attacks, boss battles and mini bosses. There’s also a really fluid cover system that a lot of triple A games could learn from.
The bad: All the levels look pretty similar. The game is relatively short, you can complete all the levels and get a max level character in under 5 hours - but, there is a lot of replayability so that helps. Online multiplayer is poorly done: no chat, random annoying people dropping in your game and no way to kick them, difficult to play with friends or make friends to play with - but, the devs are working on this and local co op is the shiznittlebambizzle. The skills are useful but don't allow customization on higher levels because you'll max out everything.
The good far outweighs the bad and the devs are still updating it so it will only get better.

Kingdom Rush is a superb take on the Tower Defence genre.  If you're a fan of tower defence games or like a casual game to play during those lazy weekends Kingdom Rush is a must.
There are several different towers like you'd suspect from a tower defence game. There is the fast shooter with low damage aka the arrow tower. Then there is the magic tower with moderate power but slow. There is also the tower that hits multiple enemies. Finally there is the melee tower that produces units to stop enemies in their tracks. You can upgrade each tower several times.
The soundtrack is decent, mixed with the hilarious lines given to each tower when you fully upgrade them makes the game just that bit better. The cartoon style graphics creates a funny entertaining view while obliterating those pesky enemies.
So why are you still reading this, buy it now :D

The early access was brilliant, better than this stable version.
Currently the game (1.0 release) has scaling issues and is quite imbalanced, underpowered towards the beginning and overpowered towards the end, with a middle game that barely exists as you try to power through planets to get to the next set of upgrades. It used to be a fun type of grind, but with the general need for more items (volume, as well as different type) to upgrade things it becomes gradually more frustrating. Although the pace for upgrading your MM and Tech feels a bit better.
The change to equipping items feels terrible, initially I thought I'd get used to it like a person normally would, but it feels too unnatural. You need to equip many items in general: melee weapon, ranged weapon, torches, rope, trash blocks, flashlight, health kits. That's mainly for exploring, even then more items can be added. And for some reason many items that you think would be single-handed are actually two-handed. Great! Even more switching to do!
The need for food to restore your hunger significantly adds to the monotony. Go out into that vast universe - and become a farmer! It does get better, but takes away from the experience nonetheless.

There's a lot to love in this game, but also a lot to hate. If you're curious but don't want to commit to cash quite yet I recommend you check out CoE2 available for free from Illwinter's site as a free download. It's a lot more limited than this version of the game, but will give you a pretty good feel for how it handles.
On the good side, if you're looking for a streamlined fantasy 4X that offers a unique collection of races and play mechanics, this might be your games (I especially enjoyed Illwinter's take on why you never see any female dwarfs). It's really satisfying to finally round up enough innocents to summon demon lords, or to finally complete the necromantic ritual which will turn you into an immortal vampire in an old, abandoned castle.
On the bad side, Illwinter doesn't really care that much about UI. In the Dominions series (which has gotten a lot better on this front) it was the price of admission for a really unique strategy game. With the stripped down CoE approach, the lapses in UI design feel a lot less forgivable. For example, there's no smooth way to start a new game without exiting and launching the game again. Unit moves can't be cued, so you spend a lot of time babysitting commanders on there way back to grab reinforcements.
Past the interface, the abundance of unfriendly fauna can get rather obnoxious. While it's cool that you need to be careful early on, by mid game marauding bands of deer taking unprotected farms just gets annoying. Commanders are a limited resource in the game, so keeping them on hand for pest control can get frustrating. Plus I'm unaware of any kind of "major events" summary, so I spend a lot of time at the beginning of each turn checking my domain and making sure Bambi isn't stirring up any trouble. Then on larger maps you can have to cross fields covered with unthreatening but still annoying spawns.
Finally, there's side balance. As is the case with any game that has 17 truly unique sides it's a nightmare. Necromancer's can be unstoppable in the Fallen Empire period, or they can get screwed by their early game position. Playing a side that relies on mines? Hope you start near some, because while your capital normally counts as one, there might not be any others nearby.

Sid Meiers Civilization 4: Colonization is an interesting beast to review, it's a remake
of the 1994 "sister game" to Civilization using the legendary Civilization 4 engine, but
remains different enough from Civilization 4 to feel like a overpriced expansion. I
should probably mention that I pretty much only play the fantastic mod "The Authentic
Colonization" which fixes a lot of issues with the base game and makes it more
challenging, but I'll try to keep the review on the actual base game (but the modding
community is amazing).
+Great graphics, way more detailed than Civ 4 and even Civ 5..which is kind of odd.
+Good soundtrack, not quite as great as the original (♫ Jine the calvary♫) or as good as
Civ 4 (Baba yetu~)
+The early game is way more active than Civ 4, you have to sail around the new world
looking for good land, the Natives will be angry if you settle to close to them and you
can't settle near Europeans at all, this adds a great deal of planning and strategy.
+The new leaderheads for the Europeans/Native Americans are fantastic, very well animated and full of personality and character, I personally think Cunhambebe has the best animations out of them all.
+Getting soldiers/scouts/pioneers (workers) is way more realistic, instead of training a unit, you actually have to equip a civilian with tools/horses/guns, and newly equipped soldiers will be weaker than battle hardened ones, it's a great system that really makes every military unit matter.
+Native variety is good, it features the Iroquois, Cherokee, Apache, Sioux, Aztecs, Mayans, Arawak, Incas and the Tupi, it could use more Amazonian tribes but other then that it's pretty good, some mods add way more such as the Inuits, Shuar, Comanche, Blackfoot, Shoshone etc.
+Awesome mods, my favorites are "The Authentic Colonization", "Colonization 2071" and "The age of Discovery II".
+/- The amount of Colonies is pretty small, just the English, French, Dutch and Spanish, all have two leaders but are pretty well balanced. Mods add a lot more leaders, such as Russians, Chinese, Danes, Portuguese etc.
+/- The game gets a little boring once you find great land and found a few cities and start to get a decent economy, but gets going again in the "mid-game" when Natives start to get ticked off at other colonies and start New World War 1.
-The warfare system stinks, it's like Civ 4 but with way less actual unit variety and can be very easy to sack enemy cities in the first few turns.
-All natives have the same unit type called "Braves" and use the same model, yes the Incas, Aztecs, Cherokee and ARAWAK look the same and the model they use is very generic looking, luckily most mods fix that and give really cool custom models for each Native.
-Game feels a bit rushed, especially is the "final battle" against your home country, just basically boils down to the king bum rushing your cities and you just kill a few of his soldiers and you win.

With groups of games it's always gonna be a mixed bag, but overall I'd definitely recommend checking out if you're a fan of retro NES games. The games were very nostalgic, while still holding up to today's standards.
Super Clew Land Complete - Didn't finish, played for 50 minutes before the shaking of the screen became too much, got a seizure from playing. :S I did enjoy what I played though, was very reminiscent games I used to LOVE as a kid.
End of Line - A really fun puzzle game. Despite the simple layout/premise still made you think. Love the graphics.
GAIAttack - Had a lot of fun with this beat 'em up. Was hard to get used to the controls at first but really addictive gameplay once I got into it. Unfortunately the game doesn't save your progress, be sure to play it in one sitting.
Paradox Lost - Mixed thoughts on this one. I like the concept and it definitely reminded me of some older games, but it got tedious at times. The novelty wore off halfway through and having to backtrack a lot and avoid getting lost was meh. The sound effects were also pretty basic/annoying. I can see why others would like this but personally wasn't my cup of tea.
Wub-Wub Wescue - Such a fun game!! If you like platformers I'd definitely recommend checking it out.  Loved the mechanic of the music boxes and jumping to the beat of the music. I will say a couple levels were a bit frustrating and finicky (mostly due to being longer levels, one little mistake and your pup not jumping where you wanted him too / the bat not reacting perfectly and you have to restart). Overall though this one was definitely a highlight of the bunch.
Brains & Hearts - Took me a little to figure this card game out, but I was determined to win. The A.I. are pretty tough so you will lose early on, but I'd rather them be too hard than too easy. It's one of those games where you don't completely love it, but it's got addicting gameplay of "just one more game". Could see myself playing this more on a phone. Still I enjoyed it and though it didn't quite fit in with the rest of the games genre-wise, it was refreshing having something different in the mix.
Shūten - Big pleasant surprise! I've not played many shoot 'em ups but after playing this it definitely made me want to check out more. Balanced difficulty, not too hard but enough to feel satisfying beating the levels. You can also customise how difficult you'd like to make it for yourself, buying the various power ups. The mobs had some predictable move paths, but I personally didn't see it as a downside. It was fun figuring out their abilities/paths and then changing your gameplay accordingly.
So yeah overall I'd recommend it! While this wasn't my favourite game of all-time, I had a good experience playing. It was really nice going on a nostalgia trip and playing some shorter, similar games to ones I used to love as a kid.

A set of six fun games styled after many of the classic action, adventure, and puzzle games of the 2D era.
Each game is long enough to explore a few variations on the core mechanic, but short enough to remain fun throughout (usually about an hour or two). These games also strike a good balance between being challenging enough to be engaging, and easy enough to just pick up and play.
The best part about these games is the design:
- Real levels. Maps are clearly designed, not randomly generated segments tossed together
- Real goals. Each game has a definite goal (not just "see how many points you can get, then try again!")
- Real endings. You can actually get the satisfaction of finishing the game before moving on to the next (no infinite levels or endless grinding in a "challenge mode")
- Real direction. You learn how to play by being put in situations that let you discover each new mechanic (no big instructions to read upfront, and no annoying interruptions mid-game telling you to press a button to do something)
Given all that, I'd happily purchase a sequel that explored another half dozen game styles.
Also, there's a card game.

I can be going through a level and doing fine, then all of a sudden two machine gunners pop up on both sides of me and no matter what gear or weapons you are using, if two machine gunners pop up close to you like that, it's game over. Any enemies spawning in on top of you like that creates a real problem in any game. Some weapons are worthless, like the flame and shotgun weapons. You will never be able to get close enough to use them without dying. You will never progress in the normal missions unless you do a lot of grinding in the wave attack mode. It seems like now though I am at lvl 50 the wave attack does not give enough exp so I have to play the regular missions and pray to God that I don't get random pop-ins on top of me during them. The wave attack + wearing the extra coin drop hat is also the only way you can get enough coins and upgrade chips to afford new weapons, upgrades, and armor. There are weapon upgrades that are also worthless but you don't know until you find out with some trial and error. The upgrade for the machine gun that gives you ammo regen is basically a requirement because without it, you will run out of ammo quickly during a level and ammo drops are rare and even when they drop only give you a few bullets. This means that you basically can't pick the upgrade next to the ammo regen unless you want to see that problem. So if that is the case, why even offer another skill?
The graphics are well done, the sound is good, the music is great dubstep, the gameplay is smooth, and the story is pretty much non-existent, just like I like it. I get quite enough story in my rpg's and books I read, I don't need it in my action games. I play action games because they are simple and I want to just blow people away. I don't want a bunch of cut scenes or text in my action games. This game is just straight up fighting.
7/10 pretty fun, although the problems I mentioned really should be addressed but obviously never will.

Игра  довольно красочная и живописная :) и как известно славится за свою жестокость фаталити и насилия, чего не найдёшь в привычных файтингах вроде Tekken или Injusties. Насилие конечно есть во всех игр данного жанра и с этим не поспоришь. Также игра может похвастаться огромным разнообразием персонажей и костюмов для них, а так же богатой сюжетной линией. Красивые движения, стойки, удары и стили ведения боя вполне удовлетворят сердца всех поклонников боевых исскуств. Игра показывает отличный гейплей, графику и т.п. Думаю Mortal Kombat не создана для того, как многие говорят "задр*тить" в неё, а для нечто большего. Немногий игрок сможет найти весь потенциал данной игрули, а только настоящий фанат. Поэтому MK создана чтобы ИГРАТЬ в неё и не многим игрокам дано такое качество, особенно касаясь МК, ведь это далеко не лёгкая игра. Что же касается всей серии игры, то данная игра- 9 часть в серии насколько мы знаем. Повторяюсь, что сюжет тут довольно интересный и многим он понравится, в него были включины почти все персонажи из прошлых серий игры. Кстати на данный момент разрабатывается МК10, который судя по немногочисленным обзором несильно отличается от описываемой 9ой игры серии. Но 9 мк мы можеи считать взлётом серии в который обязательно будут и сейчас играют многие поклонники файтинга. Что же касается управления то оно неудобно.. на ПК. В общем Mortal Kombat Komplete Edition- отличная игра. Я удостаиваю её написать о ней положительный отзыв. Игра безоговорочно заслуживает палец вверх. Всем советую.

// Mortal Kombat is a 3D Fighting Game: //
// Schuitje82 - Extended Review //
About the game:
============
What is all to say about Mortal Kombat?
People who have gotten along MK1 Arcade or Sega / Nintendo era know what this game is all about.
Amazing, bizarre characters and a cool story or not to mention hope bloody violence: P
Mortal Kombat games have many lows reached on consoles.
Lot of bad games are there that have been ruining the MK series.
Only Mortal Kombat 9 makes up for it.
For me, Mortal Kombat 9 is a complete reboot of the game.
And all characters from MK1 to MK3 come back in one big story.
Story Mode:
==========
To start story mode reflects perfectly true Mortal Kombat is about.
Many movies and you play with all the characters in the game.
Sometimes this can be very annoying because you have to get used again and again to the new characters and learning all the moves of the characters.
I prefer to play the game / story mode on the most lowest difficulty setting for the best experience from the story mode.
Ladder Mode:
==========
You also have the old arcade ladder as in the old games.
This allows you to play as single or tag mode.
Tag mode, you and your friend to battle against the computer in ladder mode. (CO-OP Mode Offline)
I find the CO-OP mode a very good extra to this game / ladder mode.
Tower Challenge Mode:
==================
Tower mode, a total of 500 challenges that are quite challenging and this can probably best to keep busy for a while.
And gives a big challenge filled with frustration.
It's really a lot of fun to play and try to find a new challenge.
Online:
======
MK9 still get played a lot when I made this review.
Main problem online has is the super big lag sometimes so horrible the game is unplayable.
So keep in mind search a player that is close to your region.
Also in online mode you have Single, Tag and King of the Hill will give you plenty of variety.
Unfortunately, King of the Hill can sometimes be a long wait and watch game long before you end up in a fight because of the many players that comes in a game.
And if 1 person has a bad connection he will ruin the gameplay / match because of the big lag he will make in the group.
So online play is not the best experience and I recommend like old times 2 or 4 player on the couch with some controllers.
Finally:
======
MK9 is a very fun game and easy to pick.
Combos are easy to learn if you take the time to do it.
Game is often on sale and would definitely try this game if you like fighting games.
And with the complete edition you then have all the extra fighters.
So no stupid DLC to buy anymore.
Only downside is.
Find a shame that the publisher is fairly stopped supporting the game for extra content.
I give this game a 9/10

Well Bethesda just knows how to build massiv interresting worlds.
This game speaks for itself.

Imagine a fusion of Just Cause 2 and Saints Row 3 where they've taken all of the open-world goodness and all of the over-the-top ridiculous humor and just left it out of the game. The game is open world in the sense that you're free to drive around the city running over rival gang members, betting on chicken fights, or helping pedestrians perform mundane tasks until you're bored enough to take on one of two missions that progress the story line.  Saddle that with a clumsy combat mechanic that sought to make use of every button on a 360 controller but went a step to far and ends up giving a Keyboard the cold sweats, and you have Sleeping Dogs.  Lets not forget the DLC... do you like Ed Hardy?  The DLC is basically the Ed Hardy catalog, you can pay full retail prices for digital representations of clothing sure to make the cast of Jersey Shore cream their shorts.
The story is your typical cop in deep cover forced to make choices between blowing is cover and crossing the line.  If you didn't pick up on where this is going one of the gang bangers is kind enough to spell it out for you in the second gang mission when he says something along the lines of "we had a guy like you, he turned out to be a cop and we found out cause cops can't kill."  Gee whiz, I have no idea where this story is going.  They even drive this fact home by dinging you XP if you cause any property damage or kill anyone during a mission.  But that's only during missions, between missions you're free to kill with reckless abandon.  There's a GTA style escalation of police response but when the cops drive up on you mid killing spree and you can prance away on foot down any street you like, you've lost any immersion you had.
The combat mechanic is atrocious; do you really need 3 melee related buttons, two of which have long press alternate functions?  There's so many buttons they needed to merge jump, sprint, and "parkour" into a single button press.  I say "parkour" because that's what they call it but it's really just jumping and grabbing, there's no gracefully skipping across roof tops like Mirror's Edge or even a Matrixesque wall run.  You want to climb a wall, step back and run at the wall holding the sprint/jump/parkour button then just before hitting said wall lift your finger off the button and press it back down.  It requires no skill and looks just as lame on screen.  This is in stark contrast to combat which is so complicated the need to resort to flashing red visual queues for everything because you're preoccupied fumbling with all of the attack, counter attack, melee, fire, and cover buttons.  It's like they wanted Street Fighter close combat but couldn't drop standard FPS dynamics, the result is a mess plan and simple.  On top of that and with all the buttons required to play, it restricts just what buttons you can bind.  Want to use the Enter key, or perhaps arrow keys?  F**K YOU!
I tried the play this game on two seperate occasions and just did not enjoy it.  Both times it crashed on me for no apparent reason and neither time was I upset, I was actually thankful and just played something else instead.
TLDR; Save your money for something else.

The AVP series returns! AVP 2(Which isnt even on steam!!) was released a whopping 9 years before this game! Thats definetely too long to be waiting!.
Anyway this game's main strong point in SP is that you have 3 campaigns to play (much like the earlier games.) Obviously you have the Path of the Predator , Alien and the Weakest of them all...Marine
This game gets lots "correct" as expected, but most are already standard this kind of series but many gameplay mechanics and controls are awkward and there are many imbalances in Multiplayer unfortunetely. But ill cover all that in the Pros and Cons below.
+Campaigns (15 hours on average)
+Many Collectibles to read (Backstry
+Hot Corporal xD
+Interesting Story for the Marine and the Predator that show very unique motivations!
+Amazing Multiplayer Modes! The three Species really combine for some real chaos! (Across 7 Gamemodes!)
+Weapons are Creative and have different "Classes" for each species too.
+A new Planet (BG-386) with about 6 Large Environments to explore. These Maps are "recreated" slightly for multiplayer but the unique feel that each one brings still remains.
+Soundtrack and General Sound clarity (Especially for the "Rookie" Marine). This mixed with the environments really help immersive the player! (Some examples of great sound effects being used include: Rocks Crumbling in the Pyramid and Ruins, Frogs, Birds and even other-worldy creatures make their calls and even Noisy Dust Storms on Barren Areas of the Surface.
+General Mechanics are very unique for each species. Some Examples include: Blood Stained Motion-Tracker HUD for the Marine, Simplified but Advanced Predator HUD with Special Symbols representing Health, Energy and even 4 View-Modes (Including the Infamous infra-Red/ Marine-Doom Vision). The Predator HUD is especially awesome though because its like an ancient language native to the species with very few icons/symbols on-screen at once, power and health only show when they are affected but the Environment/Enemies.
+Alien Traversal- Climb Everywhere! Maybe...Behind you
+Predator Traversal- "Jumpin, Jimmies! Hes fast.."
+Very Gory for players who like that sort of thing (I know i do ;D)
+Finishers in Multiplayer are amazingly creative and is more than equivalent to backstabbing someone in COD (Thats why its special!) A Short-scene will play showing the Gory finish and aftermath of the enemy you just dominated! (Similar to DooM 4...in a Way)
-The majority of maps are boring and lack interesting Features in Multiplayer. For Example, there are no items to interact with, no environmental traps or danger zones, and ZERO Light adjustments when in very dark areas! (Marine's sh*tty flashlight isnt going to do anything!!)
-Marine is so underpowered compared with the Predator, but more even when compared with the Aliens abilites. (Motion tracker was made for the Xenos!)
-Story is so short for each species. Although decent, its lacking in any effort to make the player really care for/trust/love/despise/ interested about. There are about 5 characters in the Marine story that i was interested in. Especially after reading the Logs. But Many Marine Grunts, Allies and even the main Antagonist (Lack of history about them when playing..have to rely on more logs to really understand their intentions.) Make a noticeably small impact on players. Of course this is an Action FPS but more connection with fellow squad members would be very interesting (something that Colonial Marines has instead!?)
-Speaking of Marine Grunts, the Voice Acting is repetitive and unimportant "obvious" commands can easily be ignored/misheard due to the proximity you need to be.. :(
-The Graphics are Terrible for a Game of its Reputation and time period! at 2000 and 2001 it didnt really matter about that sort of thing, but this isn't good at all!
It definetely not grainy, but instead it very glossy/reflective and doesnt handle darkness well at all. This is good for the Predator and the Alien, but once again the Marine comes off worse!
-Alien Campaign's Plot and Levels is very predictable, crawl here, escape from here, harvest those people, etc. least interesting story of the 3 but the ending is very good :D
-The Marine movements are slow and clearly Flawed when compared with the other enemies. It also suffers some painfully Bad Controls (and LACK of some controls) such as: he runs out of breath after 5 seconds of running, no crouching of prone, no ADS or Iron-Sights and he even jumps a whopping 5 centimetres in the air!
-Multiplayer unlocks (Rewards for HARD WORK)are bland and the alien skins are Very Similar, out of the 3 species youd expect the natural predator with elite organic claws and fangs to have the most variation! But only 2 of the Alien Skins really stand out (Out of 6)
-Unfortuntely there isnt enough maps to go with the large ammount of gamemodes! (It should be reversed!!)

The Aliens and Predator franchises have had there ups downs, and when combined into films it was the ladder. In gaming however they really worked! Starting back in the Arcade as a “Final Fight” style beat-em up, the Atari Jaguar in 1994, the PC version in 2000, and a sequel in 2004. All were fun games for their time. So how does the latest in the series hold up? Well it helps if your a fan of Alien, and The Predator movies, and I am so my review may be biased. The game is broken into three campaigns that tie in the main story. Players can choose a Colonial Marine, the Alien, or The Predator. Each class plays very unique with their own abilities. The Marine campaign was my favorite, it captures some of the Aliens feel. There is a great line-up of movie weapons, tense scenes, and a lot of action. My complaints for the Marine are minor. I really wish they added “Aim Down Sites”. Firing from the hip in gaming is just old school, I need my sites! Second complaint is the motion tracker, It's all but useless in the game. I know I'll get some heat for saying this, but Aliens Colonial Marines made far better use of the motion tracker. My second favorite campaign was The Predator. With all of his tools at your disposal, you will feel like an unstoppable hunter. My only complaint on The Predator is the “pred jump”. At times it can be a pain to line up, but once you know the map its less frustrating. The Aliens campaign was my least favorite. The Alien can transition to walls, and run in 3D. It has some interesting fatalities, and is extremely fast. However This is extremely disorientating in first person view, and I can't tell you how many times I ran right by an enemy because of the speed the Alien runs at. This could have been easily fixed if the Alien had 3rd person perspective. The game offers a decent amount of multiplayer modes, and a decent number of maps. The only thing I wish is there was a little more variety in the scenery. Your either in a Jungle, or a pyramid, and that’s about it. The game will run on almost any PC if you adjust the resolution, and graphics options (Not your Apple II, but anything from 2010 and up should be fine). Overall this game despite its flaws is a very fun play, and I recommend it. If you've been passing on this one, and your a fan of either franchise you should pick it up

This game had so much promise when I started backing it, and it still has so much promise.
Sadly, despite five years in development limbo, it does not deliver.
Cast your minds back, three or so years if I recall correctly. I was an innocent young lad going about my day to day business, when my friend sends me a message telling me about this new game in development. It's called "Starbound", and it looks like Terraria in space, but with so much more to it - an endless, infinite universe. I'm entranced, and I buy the crap out of it. Playing through early versions, I can tell it's rough but has promise, so much promise.
I check back every now and again, seeing how things develop. Things are looking good. I play a few hours here and there, but there always seems to be something missing. Something missing which, I assume, will eventually be added in.
Fast forward to today, and there's still something missing. I still can't quite put my finger on it. Haven't played very much of the new version, since my characters were all wiped (after being promised this wouldn't happen, but hey, these things happen).
Anyway, good things first. Starbound is a game with a fantastic atmosphere. I love the art style, the music is grand and the snarky comments on every single item in the game really pull me in to this living, breathing universe.
Sadly, everything else pulls me right out. The controls are floaty, so I fall to my death over and over again. The combat is absolutely awful (and others have already elaborated on that far better than I could). The UI is a joke, and contributes to maybe half of my (many many many) deaths as I frantically try to swap to a sword and end up limply patting my enemy with a stick of corn. I've experienced recurring lag with enemies, even though I'm playing singleplayer (I'm taken to believe this is a fairly common issue).
The universe is massive, yet so shallow that it could probably bring a tear to Todd Howard's eye (take that, Bethesda). There's no reason to stay on any planet for longer than necessary, essentially making every planet an identical "fetch what you need and move forward" half hour outing (simultaneously removing the feeling of slow-paced wonder that comes from exploration). Dungeons aren't very interesting, in my opinion. Railroaded linear quests absolutely destroy any sort of natural progression which is usually fairly necessary in an open sandbox game.
That's not to say I haven't enjoyed Starbound. There are moments of absolute brilliance tucked away in the game. Exploring new planets can be awesome if you tune out the fact that it's only cosmetically any different from the last one - the massive amount of varying art assets are a high point, and I give immense credit to the game's artists. The same goes for building a base (though in earlier versions I always used admin commands to give myself an unlimited amount of construction materials). I like the ability to make homes for settlers, and build a large town.
All in all, Starbound had so much promise. Promise that seems to have been more or less wasted in favour of working on small additions and not really working on the major 'feel' of the game, if that makes sense (I mean, spaceship pets? Really? Why?). I still have hope for the future of the game (especially with mods), but at the moment it just feels empty. I love the game, and loathe the game. I've gone on for quite a while now, so I should probably end here - Starbound is a brilliant concept badly realised. I wish the devs luck on improving it, but it seems like it's too far gone by now.
One small caveat: Starbound isn't as similar to Terraria as many are saying. For one thing, Terraria is consistently quite good.

I didn't know what to expect going into ICEY, other than it was popular for its meta-narrative, something that a few games have tried but not entirely mastered.  ICEY is certainly one of those which succeeds in this area, but if I was to simply say you ought to try this on that basis alone it simply wouldn't do the game justice.
Not only because of its simple but brilliant gameplay (superb hack and slash combat where it's easy to find a style to suit whatever niche you want to fall into) but also because of how that meta-narrative I mentioned is woven into the game itself.
If all you want to do is go through the game and have a great time beating up some quite fun enemy designs, by all means you can ignore everything else, but if you just try a dig a little deeper there is a lot more for you to find from commentary's on game production to more existential questions.  In fact it will certainly make you come back for more as you try and explore just what can be done by pushing just beyond its boundaries.
If I'm completely honest, the Meta side of things never entirely sold it for me when I played through, don't get me wrong I really thought it was entertaining, but it was the fact that it was in conjunction with everything else that made it hit a perfect sweet spot making me want to play it again.  It's not a long game, but it's certainly one that has stayed with me and given its relatively cheap price at the date of this review (22/11/2017 - £6.29) it's certainly worth picking up.

The interface is abysmal, the sound design is lackluster, the graphics are simple to put it lightly...
And if you can get past the fact that it's completely lacking any of those bells and whistles and take the time to figure out how to play, you will be rewarded with one of the most mechanically sound 4X games I've ever played. Have you ever played a Civilization game and thought "this is nice, but it's just lacking -something-, feels like it's too aesthetic-heavy, and I really wish it didn't take four days non-stop to play one game"? Try this. The pacing is excellent, each 'race' plays totally differently instead of just having one or two unique units availible only at a certain point in the game and feel fairly well-balanced in spite of it, it only takes a couple of hours to play a game through, you'll continue to have that feeling of exploration and conquest through the game instead of only at the beginning, and it even feels more like you're building an empire than Civ games because NPCs will actually put up a fight, and be genuinely lethal if you let your guard down.
So, if you'd like a 4X strategy game in an interesting fantasy setting with excellent pacing and very well executed RPG elements, give Conquest of Elysium a try, but only if you can get over games with weak graphics, sound, and interface. Great for classic roguelike players who are used to ASCII graphics and perplexing interfaces.
If you -don't- like 4X strategy games or are thinking of getting into them and looking for a springboard, just walk away now, this is not the place to start.

Functional graphics and sound aside, this game is deeply rewarding, but can be very punishing if you are impatient or not thinking strategically. A very worthwhile way to spend your time if you enjoy strategy turn-based games. Note: I've got hundreds of hours logged with COE3 on Desura.

If your looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if your looking for an outstanding pie recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients:
1. 6 tablespoons unsalted butter
2. 1/2 cup white sugar
3. 1/2 cup brown sugar
4. 1/4 cup water
5. 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
6. 1 pinch salt
7. 5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced
8. 1 pastry for double-crust pie
Directions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.
3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.
4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.
5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.
6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing.

Imagine a fusion of Just Cause 2 and Saints Row 3 where they've taken all of the open-world goodness and all of the over-the-top ridiculous humor and just left it out of the game. The game is open world in the sense that you're free to drive around the city running over rival gang members, betting on chicken fights, or helping pedestrians perform mundane tasks until you're bored enough to take on one of two missions that progress the story line.  Saddle that with a clumsy combat mechanic that sought to make use of every button on a 360 controller but went a step to far and ends up giving a Keyboard the cold sweats, and you have Sleeping Dogs.  Lets not forget the DLC... do you like Ed Hardy?  The DLC is basically the Ed Hardy catalog, you can pay full retail prices for digital representations of clothing sure to make the cast of Jersey Shore cream their shorts.
The story is your typical cop in deep cover forced to make choices between blowing is cover and crossing the line.  If you didn't pick up on where this is going one of the gang bangers is kind enough to spell it out for you in the second gang mission when he says something along the lines of "we had a guy like you, he turned out to be a cop and we found out cause cops can't kill."  Gee whiz, I have no idea where this story is going.  They even drive this fact home by dinging you XP if you cause any property damage or kill anyone during a mission.  But that's only during missions, between missions you're free to kill with reckless abandon.  There's a GTA style escalation of police response but when the cops drive up on you mid killing spree and you can prance away on foot down any street you like, you've lost any immersion you had.
The combat mechanic is atrocious; do you really need 3 melee related buttons, two of which have long press alternate functions?  There's so many buttons they needed to merge jump, sprint, and "parkour" into a single button press.  I say "parkour" because that's what they call it but it's really just jumping and grabbing, there's no gracefully skipping across roof tops like Mirror's Edge or even a Matrixesque wall run.  You want to climb a wall, step back and run at the wall holding the sprint/jump/parkour button then just before hitting said wall lift your finger off the button and press it back down.  It requires no skill and looks just as lame on screen.  This is in stark contrast to combat which is so complicated the need to resort to flashing red visual queues for everything because you're preoccupied fumbling with all of the attack, counter attack, melee, fire, and cover buttons.  It's like they wanted Street Fighter close combat but couldn't drop standard FPS dynamics, the result is a mess plan and simple.  On top of that and with all the buttons required to play, it restricts just what buttons you can bind.  Want to use the Enter key, or perhaps arrow keys?  F**K YOU!
I tried the play this game on two seperate occasions and just did not enjoy it.  Both times it crashed on me for no apparent reason and neither time was I upset, I was actually thankful and just played something else instead.
TLDR; Save your money for something else.

Comparisons to the GTA series will undoubtedly come up often while playing Sleeping Dogs and it's accurate to say that this game draws from the same well so to speak. I'll just come out and say that Sleeping Dogs is better than at least GTA4 (San Andreas is better than GTA4 as well... and I haven't had the pleasure of playing 5 yet). The vehicles handle better, the plot is far more engrossing, and the combat system is in a completely different league (they are different styles of game, to be fair. GTA relies more on guns and in Sleeping Dogs you will only have use of a weapon in a few missions).
That is not to say that Sleeping Dogs doesn't have its flaws but they aren't immersion breaking flaws and a lot of them are just down to personal preference on my part. One of the game's BEST features is the level of detail designed into it. Sleeping Dogs' Hong Kong isn't as big of an area as a lot of other open world games and the designers seem to have taken advantage of this and put as many minor details into the design as possible. The few times you enter a building, for example, they are beautifully furnished and have bits and pieces that make them seem all the more real. The hospital in Central, for example, has several doctors offices, an MRI machine, and nurses performing their rounds. All for a mission that takes about 15 minutes to complete and you will probably never go back there.
The combat system is almost flawless. You begin with a few basic combos and the ability to counter opponents strikes (which is essential to master if you want to get very far). As you progress you gain experience in Cop, Triad, Face, and Melee trees which allow you to unlock various skills including new hand to hand moves. By the time you unlock the whole melee tree you are virtually unstoppable in hand to hand combat.
A few of the things I didn't like or I find strange: They have an immense amount of music in the game; just look at the credits... but I only recall hearing the same 3 or 4 songs every time I got into a car. Sure you can flip through stations and wait to hear them all if you really want to, but driving isn't an essential part of this game like it is in GTA or Saints Row. There seems to be no easy way to get a firearm: You eventually unlock the ability to open the trunks of police cars to get a gun and if you need a gun for a mission they'll give it to you, but there are a few areas in the game that you need a gun to get through (such as 3 or 4 drug busts) that you need to bring your own gun to or you will almost certainly fail. I didn't like how the girls you "date" are basically just throwaway characters that you do one mission for and never speak to again. It makes your character seem like a total ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Sure you're a triad enforcer who murders hundreds of people in the course of the game... but I don't want to be a misogynist too. The women do eventually stand up for themselves a bit but I won't spoil that. Plus they hired Emma Stone to voice about 15 lines of dialogue... strange.
Voice acting is top notch, plenty of side quests to keep you playing even after the main campaign is over, and just the right amount of collectibles so you aren't spending a quarter of your life trying to track them down. None of the DLC are particularly necessary except for the two mission expansions but they do add some fun new weapons and buffs.
If you're a fan of this type of game, this is a must have.

As a fan of Hong Kong cinema, the way Sleeping Dogs depicts its story had me attached to the plot, characters and setting from start to finish. Every character has personality, and while there isn’t a stand out individual, each one feels developed enough for you to care about their associations with Wei and it helps that the voice acting is fantastic. The game’s length is about 15-hours with side missions extending to double that.
The first three hours of Sleeping Dogs demonstrate a lot of the improvements to the GTA gameplay with the traversal free running and hand-to-hand combat. Hand-to-hand combat is heavily inspired by the Batman: Arkham series of video games, with Wei being able to punch, grapple and counter to victory. Grappling is a rather good move in Sleeping Dogs. Not only is it used to throw people over edges or pound them to the ground, but it allows Wei to interact with environmental objects as a way to deal extreme damage.
Story missions are mainly great. Side missions are a different story. Most are fillers where you are chasing people, racing cars, beating people up, singing Karaoke, hacking, nothing all that exciting compared to the main plot. The cars handle well with their super arcade-like feel, and the gun combat is mostly solid, with Wei able to pull off bullet time when jumping over cover, helping with aiming headshots.
Having seen all the versions on display, there is no denying that the PC version of Sleeping Dogs is well above the graphics of the console version. I had all settings set to the highest (PC Specs: i5, GeForce 660ti, 8GB RAM) and the framerate kept above 60 throughout the whole game. It’s the world that makes Sleeping Dogs’ graphics stand out, with the city looking stunning with the downloaded high resolution pack, showcasing the neon lights blasting their rays across the road and glowing up the night of Hong Kong.

I almost never take the time to write a review of a steam game, most steam games I'm simply pleased with but not blown away, occasionally I'll write a positive review of a steam game I absolutely love. However, I don't believe I've taken the time to write a negative review of any steam game before this, so take all that into consideration when reading this review.
DO NOT BUY THIS GAME
Forgive the caps lock but I had to be clear, this game is a very good example of what people mean when they call a game "indie" as a pejorative. Is it lazy? Yep. Is it self congradulatory? Yep. Is it overpriced and exploitative in design such that it takes a lot of time to beat just because of bad game design choices? Yep.
Think what you will about "miminalism" but time and time again the indie community has shown that they believe it to mean "getting away with being lazy by calling it an artistic choice". This game uses solid colors like crazy, they aren't "beautifully rendered" solid colors, they are just solid colors. In every area of game design aside from the music (which is decent) this game cuts corners on production.
First of all the mechanics consist of little more than basic "avoid hazards, time jumps". The hazards are a lazy static design. Honestly, this game looks a whole lot like what a game would look like if you set out with the idea of "making the game requiring the least amount of effort to make and charging the most money you could get away with". And you might suggest this is cynical or baseless, but think of this: This game does not have an options screen. You can adjust window size before playing but once you are in, you are in. Why doesn't this game have an options screen? Pretty much every game in the past 20 years has had an options screen, but for some reason this game is "above having an options screen".
What nerve the developer must have to think so highly of this game. And now, for the coding, this game could be coded by most decent coders in a week or two. That's it! Compare that to a game like "The Binding of Isaac" a game with so much more depth and variety that most programmers couldn't even code or imagine. And take note, both games cost the same amount. That's the biggest insult is the price point. This game has THREE LEVELS. That's it, and how does the developer pad out the game with "additional content"? He adds THE SAME THREE LEVELS again but with the X axis inverted on the level.
"Mirror mode" is acknowledged as incredibly easy to do, it's one line of code most of the time, inverting a level can be done in under a minute, it is absurdly easy, that's why some games have it as a "cheat code". Here, the almighty genius of a developer thinks so much of his game that he thinks these 3 inverted levels without checkpoints constitute "new levels".
What really irks me though is that somehow some people seem to be buying into this game. Read the reviews, I can't wrap my head around it, are we really such sheep that this passes as a quality 5 dollar game? I can't imagine all those reviews are real, I don't want to believe I live in a world where so many people could be such suckers. This guy is selling the video game equivalent of snake oil and people are gobbling it up.
To everybody who loves this game, I have a suggestion: You can play games of superior quality like this online FOR FREE, google kongregate or newgrounds, or google some game jam like ludum dare where people make games in literally 3 days and the top 200 entries for any game jam will be better (and less lazy) than this game. AND they will be free. I know for a fact that this developer has made more than enough money scamming people with "minimalist" game design. The least he could do if he was going to be a lazy game designer is make it pretty. LIMBO is a pretty unremarkable game gameplay-wise, but at least it looked like the art took more that 2 seconds to make.
By this point I'd estimate most people have tuned out this review because it's quite long, but I had to make it and I had to make it long because I feel that passionately. Most of the indie game design community are very kind and selfless people they want their audience to enjoy their game. Here is the most damning thing about this game, and I truly believe it:
I don't think the developer cares if you like their game, only if you buy it.
I truly believe that, I got this game on some hefty sale and I still feel like I was ripped off. There are so many games of this and better quality online for free, this game has no art production value, very little innovation, and ONLY 3 LEVELS. It's a platformer with no art assets and only 3 levels that costs 5 bucks. Do you think a developer so selfish as to try to peddle such a scam of a game deserves any of your money?
Please do not buy this game, if for no other reason than to teach developers that they should care about their audience and not take advantage of them. Keep the indie community a better place by supporting good developers and not giving money to lazy exploitative developers such as this one.

There is a lot to this game. I've played it for a rather long time. I started to play it a lot more recently. I really like the game and where it's going. There are a lot I liked that was taken out and I like what they added in to replace some of it. The map is really big. Theres a lot of things you can do in it. Now let's go to the pros and cons.
Pros:
The game has a great sound track.
There hasn't been any game breaking bugs that I have found.
There is a lot of things to do in the game.
Theres a lot of side quests you can do. (With some pretty good rewards and if you do enouph of the outpost quests you can get a bigger ship)
You can build an entire city if you want to.
You can have pets that fight for you.
You can have crew that gives you benifits on the ship and help you in battle.
The art style is really neat.
Theres a lot of mods in the game that you can add, and it's really easy to add them.
There is a benifit to exploring. (Better weapons than what you can craft, upgrades to your matter munipulator, etc.)
The world really feels alive as if there is a reason to explore and have fun.
You can find really good loot or cosmetic items.
Theres a lot of furniture and decoration that you can find/make.
Now let's go to the cons:
The AI for your crew and pets are really bad. They constantly walk into danger.
The crew members seem to take an infinate amount of lava damage.
The crew suck in combat.
The pets aren't much better.
You can easily beat almost all the bosses.
There isn't much of a challenge.
The boss fights are very lackluster when you are at the level you are meant to be at.
All of the quests (Story and side quests (The village quests) are very repetitive It's the same thing every time with the story missions. Go to a planet look at things, return to the gate and hand in the quest, fight the boss, repeat. The quests that you find on planets (villages) are also very repetitive, but you get crew out of it. The quests at the outpost are pretty interesting.)
When you progress through the game it seems like you are always 1 level higher than the enemies even if you are 3 levels below them.
If you are looking for a challenge you won't really find one here.
The pet system is not good. To catch a "pet" simply hit them until they are at 50% HP then through a capture pod at them. Now you have your pet.
You can put collars on your pet, but there doesn't seem to be a way to take it off.
You can put EPP upgrades on your EPP, and like with the pets you can't take it off and when you replace it with a new one it destroys it.
Overall There is a lot of good and bad with the game. I really love the game and I have played it for a very long time. The game has changed so much from it's beginning. I recommend you buy this game if you want to. It really is a good game with an amazing sound track. Also you can play music via the instruments they have, and you can add your own music to play on them. All of this is from what I have experienced from the game.

A perfect example as to why you should NEVER leave a pixel artist as the head developer for an entire game. This game used to be an incredibly fun and rewarding sandbox game that had an identical charm with that of Terraria with tons of unique content, all to be explored in a sandbox setting with the only limitation being how much fuel your ship has, which you personally had to get before.
What is it now? A grindy, unsatisfactionary mess that somehow manages to feel linear with an hour + long bulky "tutorial" played out in an intro cutscene followed by you warping down on an earth-like planet, having the game hand-hold you through it as your ship AI spams you everytime you pick up or see something new. Along with that, they've also removed massive amounts of content from the game, including mechs, enemies, ore and bosses and now you can no longer tamper with dungeons whatsoever while before, you could dissect them and re-build awesome-looking (and functioning) things using the stuff you took on your own base, even on your own ship. No more.
The forum crying community has managed to drive this once glorious game it into the ground so hard, over 3 of my friends that used to love early versions of this game no longer want to even consider touching it with a 10-foot pole and while you as a newcomer may be neglectful of what you've missed out on, you should by no means of the imagination lower your expectations of video-games to accept the mediocrity and failure of this one.
R.I.P Starbound.

It can be semi-interesting to find the different endings, but the narrator is just so, so lame.

SUMMARY:
ICEY is a good fighting game, if samey, short, and constantly interrupted by an infuriatingly annoying narrator.
If you overlook the story, abysmal narration, lackluster story (especially the 'true ending'), it's an alright game. Graphics are great, mechanics are tight, and the game otherwise functions fine even if the levels are incredibly lazily designed.
POSITIVE:
- Graphics are great. Lots of impressive looking effects.
- Tight controls, even for a game designed for controllers (I think.)
- Fighting mechanics work well with eachother and allow for great improvement.
NEGATIVE:
Heavy spoilers below.
The game's 'meta' aspect (Is it really a meta twist if you advertise it openly?) is that if you don't do what the narrator says, he'll rant at you in overly drawn out, annoyingly spoken, and trite dialogue that mostly manifests itself as developer fury at your decision to go in the opposite direction of an arrow for the 20th time. For instance, if you choose not to kill a certain defenceless opponent, you'll be spared fighting the next (quite difficult) boss in exchange for being forced to listen to AN ACTUAL THREE MINUTES (TIMED) OF "WHY DON'T YOU DO THIS THING I TOLD YOU TO DO.", which pales in comparison to the 10-12 minutes you spend listening to him yell at you and hum classic rock tunes to himself if you say you're not ready to fight the final boss. The entire game would've been so much better if they cut the meta narration, all the minute-long speeches, and instead focused on the side-narrative of the King in Yellow which never really came to fruition except as a strangely contrived abrupt metaphor for the 'ICEY is alive now' thing at the end.
I can't say much for the game's music, as about halfway through the game I muted ICEY's volume and played Cave Story music over it instead so I wouldn't have to listen to the narrator. I don't really remember it being anything special.
The game's early levels are nicely designed, with beautiful backgrounds and well-placed enemies. This ends abruptly in the last two levels. The last level takes as long to get through as the rest of the game, because it is the rest of the game. The last level is composed of the previous levels stitched together with reskinned enemies, usually with a CRT effect put over the room; at least 3 of these rooms have the early bosses slapped into them.
The true ending made me want to shoot myself. The narrator being an AI was hinted at, so it's passable and is treated reasonably - but the big twist that when the narrator strips you of your control of ICEY, she becomes sentient, defeats the enemies, and essentially professes her love for you but laments that you can't be together because she's virtual. It's something about of a cheap anime, which I suppose isn't surprising considering the game's style.
I beat the game on hard, got all the achievements, as well as the true ending so I will never have an excuse to play it again. I even had a friend watch me play it, and he told me that going through the final level was actually painful to watch. While I'm happy for what ICEY means for the Chinese game industry, I can't in good faith suggest it.

Honestly, the story feels like its trying to be meta and cool, but it just flops with some weird whiny narrator story. "ICEY follows the arrow" "Kill Judas" "Why didn't you follow the arrow!" You will seriously here these lines 20+ times, and that is no exaggeration.
I feel like if there was no narrator, exploration for extra bosses was a reward for looking around, and that you could maybe find secret skills, then maybe this game could have been good. There was actually one scene where the narrator said "I could have added a cool use monsters attack gimmick, and was even planning to impliment a gun weapon! But couldn't cause moneyyyyyy, buy another copy plox lol" I get its a joke, but I seriously was thinking the rest of the game that if he didn't waste time on this stupid meta thing he was going for with side minigames and pointless areas that he could of easily done that. Also, because the narrator basically yells at you for exploring side areas, I eventually gave up and just wanted to finish the game. I usually like exploring, but this whole stupid narrator thing made me not want to.
All in all, I don't recommend this game. An otherwise interesting hack and slash game with high potential ruined by a developers desire to try to be meta and cool with the youngsters.

CONQUEST OF ELYSIUM3 is a great 4X game that has some roguelike elements. COE3 doesn't really have a story; all you need to know is that you have to destroy the capital city of the other players. COE is a turn based 4X game which means that you really have to think through you moves. You can assign armies and those armies can move around freely across the map. If you move one a tile that provides any sort of resources you’ll conquer that tile. If enemies are on such a tile you have to fight the opponent’s army before conquering the tile. With your new resources you can build more troops and with those new troops you can repeat the process. Compared to other 4X games COE3 is rather easy and doesn't acquire a lot of learning although a tutorial is completely missing. I got all the information i needed to play the game through the manual. It sucks that there is no tutorial because I think every game should have some explanation on how it works. But that's actually the only coplaint I have. Another great feature are the races you can play as. They all have different abilities and that spices the game up. I would recommend COE3 to everyone who likes 4X games.

With time strategy games have become more complex.  They have become more micromanaged, and these complexicites have provided more immerisive levels of game play.  However Conquest of Elysium 3 provides a simplified experience that is great in its own way.  Each class of hero (from which there are 16) the player has to choose from has a very different style of gameplay from the other classes.  This includes classes that are seeming similar, however you will find each play through, according to the class will be very different according to what could seem to be small nuiances.  If random maps and events are your thing there is no shortage here (not to mention moding options that can increase the factions and randomness).  Other than that you pick units to purchase with gold, and according to your class your unique resource (herbs, Sacrifices, Crystals; etc.) that allow you to purchase unique units or spells.  Combat is automatic; the only control you have is spells memorized by casters and the units entering the battle.  This is a great game and I caught it on a steam sale for a couple bucks, and I definitely recommend Conquest of Elysium 3 without reservations.

Each of the games is on the upper-end of the scale for what you'd expect out of a free flash game found by the dozen on sites like Kongregate and Nitrome, if not slightly longer. Also a minus: Some games have very poorly mapped keyboard controls you can't remap.
The longest games are maybe good for a little over an hour, the shortest maybe 15 mintues. The concepts behind some of them are interesting, but most are fundamentally flawed in some way. And they're also all pretty easy. So I was fine playing this when I got this free in a bundle, but I don't recommend dropping $10 on it. (Don't let my play time fool you, the game reopens itself when you close the minigame and I didn't notice so I probably only played for half that time)
Super Clew Land: Decently fun platformer wrapped around a not-well-thought-out minigame. Ok but nothing you'd miss.
End of Line: The only one I'd say is good without any qualifiers. A puzzle game with a unique premise executed well. If they were all this fun I would probably be giving the pack a thumbs up.
GAIAttack: Mindless but beat-em-up, kinda fun but shortlived. Health items and things that I assume are a score multiplier are given completely at random, which is weird. Some parts feel unfair but you have infinite lives unless you're playing for score (which seems insane in a game with this much randomness).
Paradox Lost: To contrast Super Clew Land, a fairly good concept wrapped inside a terrible Metroidvania. Worth exploring until the♥♥♥♥♥♥easy "final boss" just for the concept, but I've never seen a game before where backtracking is this painful.
Wub-Wub Wescue: An ok puzzle platformer idea, but it's designed to kill you for advancing faster than a snail's pace. So it gets boring real fast.
Brains & Hearts: Feels really out of place next to the other offerings, it's a 1v1 card game. Rules are complicated and the AI is really good at it, so it feels unfair at first but is probably better if you stick at it. Not really my thing.
Shuten: A shoot-em-up with mind-numbingly simple bullet patterns. No ammount of giving the player unusual abilities is gonna make up for tanky bosses with a single easily-dodged pattern they repeat until death. Bad.
Great selection, games are pretty good. Recommend it for the nostalgia.

Really minimal retro game.. Hard arcade

For fans of Metroid, you can travel across three time periods and the map changes accordingly.

A hint of bullet hell, you are a ninja warding off spirits and oni. Nice shop system for upgrades.
I really recommend this, it has something for everyone

Hello,
This game is the first in the series of left 4 dead games, and has largely been overtaken by the release of left 4 dead 2. There is however still enough of a playerbase for you to jump on at any hour of the day and organize a full group (4 players).
Despite what you may have read, left 4 dead 2 is not exactly the "same game" as left 4 dead, there are many differences, such as the assortment of enemies and overall gameplay.
Left4dead is much more pure and vanilla, it has 4 primary special infected instead of the 8 in left4dead2, no melee weapons and less map event triggers/sidequests.
It would be accurate to classify Left4dead2 as an updated version of this game, but with that you're losing the simplistic gameplay of the first, for a much more contrived chaotic version of itself.
As far as the gameplay goes:
- This is NOT entirely what I would consider a survival game, it is not team based Resident-Evil, it is an episodic action shooter.
- It is a team based game, while it is possible to operate solo within a map, you're more or less dependant upon those you play with, whether its AI or PC's.
- The graphics and sounds effects are good for when it was released, no complaints there.
- Level layouts are done pretty well, there are always a few bonus areas to explore, you will never find you're stuck wondering where to go or what to do, but because of this the game feels largely linear... I suppose this was the intention of the creators as it is broken down into goal oriented episodes/chapters, as a result this game can start to feel rather repetitive after playing through a particular map a few times.
- The game is never boring, it is constantly throwing enemies at you, and you're constantly rushing to finish the current map, there is very little "downtime" other than the starts and ends of each map.
- There are also two different modes of play offered apart from the regular "movie" mode. Survival, where you have to survive in a set location for as long as possible while the difficulty increases and Versus mode, where one team takes control of the zombies as the other team works its way through the map.
- There can be a few bugs in the game, such as those regarding players falling off buildings and teammates attempting to rescue them, but largely the game is not full of any bugs that directly affect gameplay.
- Personally I feel both L4D & L4D2 should have more weapons, but you never get bored with what you're given.
- Regular zombies in this game are "runners" they're not the classical slow / shuffling Romero zombies, headshots are not required to kill them. In fact these are not "zombies" at all, they're infected/mutated humans, so shooting anywhere can result in a kill.
- The amount of zombies/infected is determined largely upon the players movement through the map, there is no significant set amount of zombies within each map, player progress results in map triggers that spawn hordes of infected that rush to the players location. So moving slow, keeping quiet , etc will be of no real benefit if you're trying to avoid detection.
- It has a few additional items one would expect, med kits, pain pills, molotovs, pipe bombs, gas cans and propane tanks...all spread out rather liberally across any map, irregardless of difficulty, although it does significantly change in expert mode.
- The game offers various difficulty levels, the difficulty level does not affect regular zombie health, instead it changes the the DMG they inflict on a player when hit. Special infected on the other hand are given HP & DMG increases. With each increase in difficulty the available additional items, weapons and ammo on a given map will decrease. If you're wanting to play this as a "survival" game, setting the difficulty to "Expert mode" may offer the play experience you're seeking.
- L4D & L4D2 also seem to have a large map making community, so there will always be something new you can decide to download and play through.
- This series is not ignored by the company Devs, and they don't hesitate to fix problems or show community support.
I would recommend buying L4D/L4D2 as a bundle, if you're interested in playing. If you're seeking community numbers I would not advocate purchasing this game over L4D2, as most L4D players have migrated there.
If you enjoy team based gameplay and blasting away zombies to the point of nausea, then this is probably the game for you.
These are well made games that are supported by their company, you will never feel as if you had wasted your money, even if you don't particularily like the game.
Enjoy :)

Overiview: Isometric shooter
The Good:
+ Kill lots of enemies and upgrade you character and weapons
+ Plenty of weapons/armor/accessories to fit your play style, each piece of equipment is upgradable
+Wave attack mode is the funniest mode the game offers.
+ Good controls
+ The music is phenomenal and is probably the highlight of the game
The Bad:
-The game is built around grinding, if you want to get any of the achievements you will be grinding areas over and over again. What if you don't care about achievements? Then the game will offer no more than 30 minutes to an hour of enjoyment because there really isn't a whole lot to do in the game
-You have to replay areas over and over again because in order to upgrade and unlock weapons you need coins, something that takes a while to collect. There are accessories to help collect coins faster but that still doesn't make up for the fact that it takes a while to collect enough coins to buy upgrades and buy the weapons you want. It seems like such an artificial hurdle to pad the game length for no reason.
- As you kill enemies you gain xp to upgrade your character. You have a total of 55 levels and it becomes incredibly easy to upgrade your character, One online wave attack mode with a few people and you can easily level up 10-15 times depending on how far you get or how many people are playing. Because you can max out every skill, you don't have to make any difficult choices on how you develop your character.
-The game offers 30 levels and they all look and play the same. Every level is linear and you simply kill enemies until you reach the end. Rinse and Repeat.   As I said earlier, wave attack mode is the only fun thing in the game.
-The game froze on me one too many times.
Conclusion
The core of the game is solid, it controls really well and it has a lot of solid ideas, the problem is the developers didn't really build a game around those ideas. The upgrade/character development is horribly balanced and with some rebalancing and improvements I can see this game being a lot better. This game is an ios port and it shows and is a perfect example of what works well on one platform may not work well on others.  As it stands, I cannot recommend this game, there just isn't enough content to justify a purchase.

I'm a big fan of rhythm games, but this one does need to be recognized as a niche target audience.
The fairly steady technopunk(i'm not sure of the exact musical flavor) rhythm and enough checkpoints keep the game from being overly challenging. Instead of rushing through (which will certainly result in several deaths), most sections of all the levels almost REQUIRE you to pause and wait for the path to become clear. In some ways this is enjoyable, as it emphasizes the mental reasoning over twitch reflexes, but it can also come across like driving down a highway and hitting every light red; even if there is absolutely no rush, it gets frustrating.
Everything in the game is responsive to different track sections that the player activates to progress through the game, but the caveat to this is that while the level is perfectly in time with the music, this actually requires the character to move OUT of sync with that same music. Instead of jamming to the beat, you're really jamming in counterpoint, almost like you are actually fighting against the track. This isn't necessarily a bad thing, but for those who have grown up on or mastered DDR, Guitar Hero, Elite Beat Agents, or even games like Audiosurf or the Bit Trip series, will find themselves getting a number of annoying flase starts when they try to move to the music and match it's timing.
The controls are smooth, and incredibly simple. This could easily translate to a smartphone, using the gyroscope for movement and a single button press to jump, or the bottom half of the screen split for left and right movement, with the entire top half of the screen as a big jump button that the thumb for the inactive direction can press.
It only has 3 levels, which are then recycled into mirror levels that strip out all the checkpoints for extra challenge. There are "Boss battles" and I really enjoyed the first and second battles for these, but the final boss battle made the mistake of increasing its challenge by making it the player's ability to control their avatar more difficult, instead of making the boss smarter, tougher, or less predictable.
Due to the small size, lack of opportunity for quirky/creative acheivements (all the current steam list that are merely "beat X level" even the hidden ones) that would add to replay value, I wouldn't really recommend paying more than $2 - $3 for it, preferrably on something like a humble bundle sale that would let you get it for multiple platforms. All the same, I DO recommend it.
What this game really needs is a mixer level, that would let the player gather together and manually activate all of the different track section they had been able to aquire. This would easily add $2 to the total I'd be willing to recomend.
